lead: Dutch municipalities want to be able to exclude foreign technology from their new joint procurement of laptops, smartphones and other workplace hardware if cybersecurity or national security interests call for it. title: Cabinet wants to scrap deduction for healthcare costs, but you can still get money back until 2028: here's how it works
lead: The cabinet wants to scrap the deduction for extra healthcare costs such as orthopaedic insoles and travel costs to the hospital as of 1 January 2028. Until then, under certain conditions, you can still deduct these costs on your tax return, so you pay less tax. To do so, you do have to keep track of and fill in a lot yourself. But don't let that put you off, experts say.

title: Relief here: funding for Nedersaksenlijn, Eindhoven station and Haringvliet bridge

That comes at the expense of other wishes, but in several regions there is cause for celebration. A selection.

title: Train traffic between Rotterdam and Delft at a standstill until Sunday evening after arson
lead: It is not possible to travel by train between Rotterdam Centraal and Delft Campus until Sunday evening at the earliest. That is what ProRail reports. The <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> hopes, among other things, to learn more from camera footage about the arson at the railway last night. Why a fire was set in a technical room at a railway bridge in Delfshaven in Rotterdam is still unclear.

title: Same mania, but this seems to be the difficult second album for Tramhaus after all
Two dead in major accident with cars and trucks on N48 near Zuidwolde
lead: In a collision on the N48 near Zuidwolde in Drenthe, two truck drivers lost their lives. Three trucks and three cars were involved in the accident, confirms the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity>. The road is closed in both directions until the morning.

title: Cyclist Nooijen secures overall victory in Eneco Tour in final stage
lead: Cyclist Lieke Nooijen has secured her overall victory in the Eneco Tour. Belgian Marthe Truyen won the 70-kilometre final stage in Arnhem, but there were no large time gaps. Dutch champion Nooijen finished with a 32-second lead in the general classification over fellow countrywoman Femke Markus.

title: In this Hungarian museum, Orbán's view of history is being adjusted: 'Tackle the exhibition with a flamethrower'
Australian parliamentarian seriously injured after collision: 'This was no accident'
lead: Australian parliamentarian Helen Haines was run over by a 43-year-old man on Monday. According to Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, it was a deliberate attack. Haines has been in critical condition since the incident.

title: Woman found dead in home in Beek en Donk, police suspect a crime
lead: In Beek en Donk, the police found a dead woman in a home during the night from Friday to Saturday. One person has been arrested. The police have a 'strong suspicion' that this is a crime.

title: France and Britain expand and modernise their nuclear weapons arsenals
New York politician and 72 others released by Israel after arrest during olive harvest
Boswijk: forced departure of businesses for the military expansion of Lelystad Airport necessary, but 'worthless'
lead: State Secretary <entity id="person:derk-boswijk">Derk Boswijk</entity> calls it 'simply a worthless story' that four farms and six other businesses must make way for the expansion of Lelystad Airport, which is needed to be able to station F-35 fighter jets there.

title: These are the most fun free parties during the Amsterdam Dance Event
One in twenty Dutch people lose money after clicking on wrong links
lead: If there was financial damage, it is so far within limits. For over two thirds, reckless clicking cost at most €250.

title: Dutch roads and rail do not meet NATO requirements for transport in wartime
lead: The Dutch road and rail network, especially the bridges, is unsuitable for large military transports in many places. Military personnel and equipment can always reach their destination, but the consequences for daily traffic in a wartime scenario will be large.

title: This lawyer couple opens a second coffee shop, now in Oost: 'My mother, brother and sister-in-law are also pitching in'
'During the First World War there was a lot of appreciation for men who took on women's roles'
lead: Director Lukas Dhont, the 35-year-old Belgian darling of the Cannes Film Festival, directed the First World War drama Coward, about male love in the trenches.

All candidates for UN leadership receive veto at sixth informal straw poll, Costa Rican economist slightly favoured
Eleven people taken to hospital after tasting brewing water during Grolsch tour
lead: During an incident at the Grolsch brewery on Saturday afternoon, eleven people became ill after drinking brewing water. They were taken to hospital. "They had complaints, became nauseous and had to vomit." The <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> is investigating.

title: 'Wildwood' is in every respect impressive: technically, in terms of scale, but above all emotionally
lead: Stop-motion film Wildwood, from the studio Laika (Coraline, Missing Link), is a modern fairy tale in which the magical forest forms the backdrop to a battle between good and evil.

title: Twee mensen aangehouden in Almere voor miljoenen witwassen en hypotheekfraude
lead: De Fiscale Inlichtingen- en Opsporingsdienst (FIOD) heeft dinsdag twee personen uit Almere aangehouden op verdenking van witwassen met miljoenen euro's en hypotheekfraude.

title: Academic freedom is important enough to be mentioned in the Constitution
lead: Now that autocratic leadership is gaining ground in the world, the Netherlands would do well to think ahead and also introduce safeguards for situations that now seem hard to imagine.

title: ECB agrees to UniCredit's takeover of Commerzbank
lead: The approval from the banking supervisor in Frankfurt clears an important hurdle in the integration of the German financial institution.

title: Aanvragen voor professionele ratbestrijding nemen sterk toe in Nederland
lead: Aanvragen voor professionele ratbestrijding in Nederland zijn dit jaar sterk toegenomen, waarbij ratten goed zijn voor 12.9 procent van alle vragen over ongediertebestrijding.

title: Super-fast internet is gaining ground, but many households can make do with less
lead: More and more households have an internet subscription with high internet speed, but many people can perfectly well manage with a lower internet speed. Nearly half of all fixed internet subscriptions now offer speeds of at least 300 megabits per second.

title: The hot potato: who isn't skirting around it?
Amsterdam asks minister for plan to treat crack addicts
lead: Amsterdam is asking minister <entity id="person:sophie-hermans">Sophie Hermans</entity> of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-volksgezondheid-welzijn-en-sport">Volksgezondheid, Welzijn en Sport</entity> to quickly provide clarity on the halting of a study into a medicine for people with a severe crack or cocaine addiction. Mayor <entity id="person:femke-halsema">Femke Halsema</entity> and alderman Alexander Scholtes of Zorg write in a letter that they want Hermans to bring the parties involved together before 1 November to look for a solution.

title: The top gymnasts are no longer just teenagers: at the World Championships in Ahoy, Sanne Wevers (35) goes for the final
Zoë Papaikonomou (44) rewrites news headlines: 'It is not an asylum crisis, but a reception scandal'
Financial education
lead: Talking together about money and what you can do with it helps. So that we learn to make sensible considerations, writes FD columnist Milou Brand.

Measuring the value of art in frikandellen keeps 'Tussen kunst en kitsch' priceless television
For one day, surgeon Hoogendoorn is assistant to nurse Van der Hout: 'You get to know each other better'
Bontenbal in Brussels: faith is growing
lead: Suddenly a cheerful face appears around the corner of a meeting room in the Brussels five-star Sofitel hotel. It belongs to CDA party leader Henri Bontenbal (43). Naturally, the Rotterdam-born man is happy that Feyenoord won the evening before against the Italian club Como. Convincingly, moreover. 'Against AZ it was good too,' he adds. Bontenbal feels that Feyenoord is growing as a collective by the week.

title: Why Yesilgöz is not panicking now that the VVD is taking hits
lead: We are going to talk about bridges, roads and tunnels. Because <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> must do two things at once: make sure our road network does not collapse, and cut spending at the same time. We explain how that can work.

title: American teen (18) suspected of plotting terror attack on large shopping centre
lead: In the United States, an 18-year-old teenager has been arrested on suspicion of plotting a terror attack on a large shopping centre in Minnesota. He had bought an AK-47 rifle from an undercover FBI agent.

title: Even a fall is complicated with this minority cabinet
lead: New elections could well be far away. After all, when does a minority cabinet actually fall? Political traumas from the past are weighing on <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity>-Jetten, but at the same time stand in the way of a breakthrough. Political reporter Hans van Soest writes weekly about Hague affairs that concern us all.

title: Two dead and two injured in accident on N233 near Kesteren
lead: Two people died on Sunday in a traffic accident in the Gelderland town of Kesteren, the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> reports. Two others were injured and taken to hospital.

title: Birthday boy Ben van Bilzen (80) has been washing the NAC shirts for 55 years: 'What am I supposed to do at home now?'
lead: He doesn't drink alcohol, breathes modesty and is a model of stability. Ben van Bilzen, equipment manager for 55 years, contrasts with NAC in everything. Yet this Tuesday, on his 80th birthday, he is again the first one at the stadium. 'Whether I love it? What did you think?'

title: Di-rect singer Marcel Veenendaal (44): 'Every year they ask if I want to do The Passion. No way, I call it Depression'
Minister on rabbits that will get the Port of Rotterdam off the nitrogen deadlock: 'Sounds a bit crazy, yeah'
lead: Rabbits help get the Port of Rotterdam off the nitrogen deadlock early next year. "That may sound a bit strange at first," says Minister of Agriculture <entity id="person:jaimi-van-essen">Jaimi van Essen</entity>. Yet it is indeed part of the approach to ensure that permits can again be granted for building houses and expanding industry. "Rabbits help with that too."

title: Language skills need to improve: at this school they know how
lead: Dutch children are reading worse and worse. At the Bohemen Kijkduin primary school in The Hague, they are looking for ways to make learning to read fun.

title: Lawyer for Romy W. lashes out during closing argument: 'I am disgusted by what is happening here'
lead: The assize trial in Ghent concerning the death of toddler Dean Verberckmoes (4) is nearing its end. Today the defense of the accused Dave De K. (39) and his Zeeland-Flemish ex-girlfriend Romy W. (29) will speak first. Later in the day the jury, made up of twelve citizens selected by lot, will consider whether Dave and Romy are guilty. Follow all developments in this article.

title: Nine dismissed FBI agents who investigated Trump file complaint against director and want their jobs back
lead: Nine former FBI agents filed a complaint on Thursday against the director of the American security service, Kash Patel. The agents were involved in the investigation into classified documents that Donald Trump allegedly kept unlawfully, and were dismissed earlier this year. Follow all developments in the United States via our liveblog.

title: Wider platforms and new switches in Meppel to reduce disruptions and save 45 seconds of travel time
Cars will report exactly what happened in an accident, even before emergency responders have arrived
lead: Next year, cars will send crucial information in the event of an accident. Even before the fire brigade or ambulance has arrived, the emergency responders will know where people are in the car, whether airbags have been deployed, and whether the doors can still open. This information will also be made visible with images.

title: Cabinet does not yet rule out support for struggling seal shelter
lead: State Secretary <entity id="person:silvio-erkens">Silvio Erkens</entity> (Animal Welfare) understands the concerns about the struggling Wadden Sea World Heritage Centre (WEC). He does not yet rule out that the cabinet will step in, but does distinguish between saving the centre itself and preserving the research and rescue function for seals. That is what the VVD state secretary said in a House of Representatives debate.

title: Albert Heijn app back online, ordered groceries up to and including Thursday cancelled
lead: Albert Heijn has put its own website and app back online after the IT problems last week. The delivery drivers will 'gradually hit the road again' from Friday, Albert Heijn says. "This unfortunately means that all online ordered groceries up to and including Thursday 22 October will be cancelled."

title: The man pointed at the sleeping lion: 'A wimp. The previous one, now that was a lion. That one could roar'
Clever hornets
Rapper Appa sentenced to community service for doxxing a Jewish woman and journalist
lead: Rapper and activist Appa has been sentenced to community service of forty hours, twenty of which are suspended. The 43-year-old Amsterdammer doxxed a Jewish woman and a journalist of the NOS.

title: "Gênante" leaked email exchange between government members reveals friction within the Trump team
Diddy transferred to another prison, he 'lived like a VIP' in his cell
lead: American rapper Sean Combs, better known as Diddy, has been transferred to another prison. Various media report this, including NBC News , based on a spokesperson for the Bureau of Prisons (BoP).

title: Rain causes spectacular cyclocross race: fired-up winners receive large and heavy cheese as prize
lead: Rain and slippery conditions turned the 26th Nacht van Woerden into a true spectacle, attended by thousands of spectators. Tumbles and slips were the order of the day. Even the eventual winners Marie Schreiber (23) and Joris Nieuwenhuis (30) could not stay upright, nor could world champion Lucinda Brand. It made for an engaging spectacle in both categories.

title: Laura van Dolron once again presents a contagious inventory of everything she loves
lead: Following the success of her show 'Liefhebben' from 2014, Laura van Dolron has now made a second part. Trembling and unarmored, she shares everything that moves her, in order to create an 'upward spiral of love'.

title: Teacher's Day
lead: From the <entity id="org:gemeente-amsterdam">gemeente Amsterdam</entity>, my colleagues and I will receive a small gift to mark Teacher's Day.

title: Trump: 'US could burn like France if the Democrats win'
lead: President Trump, during an election rally, pointed to the violent protests in France. According to Trump, such a scenario could also happen in the US if the Republicans do not win in the midterm elections in early November. The president did not provide evidence for this. Follow all developments in the United States via our liveblog.

title: Max Verstappen puts on a little show at his GTWC debut, strong teammate gets in the way of podium chances
lead: Max Verstappen finished ninth on his debut in the GT World Challenge Europe. The Dutchman showed his strength, but a podium place did not materialise. Compatriot Morris Schuring did finish on the podium. Legend Valentino Rossi also took to the track in the Portuguese city of Portimão.

title: Does the flu shot protect well and isn't natural immunity better? Your questions answered
lead: Flu may seem harmless to many people, but according to the <entity id="org:rijksinstituut-voor-volksgezondheid-en-milieu">RIVM</entity>, an average of around 4.000 people in the Netherlands die every year from the effects of flu. Now that the 'season' is starting again, we asked what you wanted to know about the flu shot.

title: The real maintenance backlog in infrastructure lies in information management
lead: Our country needs to catch up on renovating infrastructure. A lot of information about existing roads and bridges was lost over the past decades or is stored in fragmented form. That needs to be tackled first.

title: No four beers from Jetten for students
lead: The higher interest on student debt caused panic among students. The question is whether that panic is justified and how much the promised cap of <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity>-Jetten actually delivers for students.

title: Amsterdam’s tastiest spring rolls according to chef Tessa Yến Nguyễn
At this Amsterdam book club, the focus is mainly on getting to know new people, with the book as the icebreaker: 'The shared interest in reading helps'
Man falls into 3-metre-deep underground container hole in Den Bosch
lead: A man fell into the hole of an underground waste container in Den Bosch on Monday morning while it was being emptied. The valves meant to close the hole may not have been working properly, the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> confirms, based on reporting by the Brabants Dagblad .

title: Jetten defends the Criminal Court after US sanctions, wants an 'appropriate solution'
lead: Prime Minister <entity id="person:rob-jetten">Rob Jetten</entity> says that the Netherlands stands firmly behind the International Criminal Court (ICC) after the new sanctions the US is imposing on the court. He calls the American measures 'very regrettable' and wants to discuss this with the American government.

title: Podcast | The cabinet's new 'offer': 'VVD seems to have given up on it'
lead: The cabinet suddenly came up with a new 'offer' for <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> to still reach a deal on the budget. But alongside relief, there was irritation about the details of the plans.

title: Gerri Eickhof kept doubting himself for 37 years: 'Maybe I'll be found out again'
lead: For years, former NOS reporter Gerri Eickhof was a familiar face in living rooms across the Netherlands. For thirty-seven years he reported on news events at home and abroad. In his recently published biography Hoe het puntje van de I op mijn hoofd viel, he looks back on his career. In De Perstribune, Eickhof talks about his insecurity, the impact of his work and the freedom he has experienced since retiring.

title: Live Eredivisie | IJssel derby at half-time with unlucky Zwolle and efficient Go Ahead
lead: Good day and welcome to this liveblog! I, Bram Schutte, will keep you informed about all Eredivisie football this Sunday. Enjoy!

title: Bosz 'proud' of PSV after Champions League win against FC Porto
lead: PSV coach Peter Bosz is "proud" of his team after the 1-0 win against FC Porto in the Champions League. The coach said this to Ziggo Sport after the match in Portugal. "I thought we played well", said Bosz. It was the first win this Champions League season for the champion of the Netherlands.

title: Closing Time | Punch
lead: Following that extremely repulsive spectacle at Cornell University, I recently saw some music by angry women pop up on social media. Hardcore punk is of course extremely well suited to a bit of justified anger. Punch is a group from San Francisco, Worth More Than Your Opinion is from their latest album from 2014. Read more posts on Sargasso

title: Champions League standings | Feyenoord just below the line after defeat in Seville, PSV mid-table and two clubs unbeaten
lead: PSV climbed to eighteenth place in the Champions League standings thanks to their win over FC Porto. Feyenoord lost away to Real Betis and are now 26th. Only the top 24 go through to the knockout phase after eight matchdays. See the full standings above and the PSV and Feyenoord fixtures below.

Mark Boumans new chair of gymnastics federation
lead: Mark Boumans has been appointed chair of the Royal Dutch Gymnastics Union (KNGU). He takes office on 1 November, the federation announces in a press release. Boumans will soon step down as <entity id="pos:burgemeester-doetinchem">burgemeester van Doetinchem</entity>.

title: 'That my group 7 pupils are in their growth spurt does not mean you can just ride your e-bike into them'
Misleading humor is an effective political weapon
lead: Misleading humor is an effective political weapon, says Beer Prakken. He earned his doctorate with research into humor in political debate. 'Someone like Trump mobilizes and radicalizes his following with humor and ambiguity.' And how about us?

title: Jack-in-the-boxes
Netherlands wants to save emergency oil stocks, but pressure to release more is growing
lead: The International Energy Agency (IEA) meets on Thursday to discuss whether countries should release more oil and oil products from their emergency stocks. The Netherlands does not want to do this for now. <entity id="org:regering">De regering</entity> fears the reserves will be needed more urgently later if the global oil crisis worsens.

title: Dave De K. found guilty of kidnapping and killing Dean (4) in Neeltje Jans
lead: A special court in Belgium on Friday found Dave De K. guilty of manslaughter and kidnapping Dean (4) in 2022. De K.'s ex-girlfriend Romy W. was acquitted of attempted kidnapping. Sentencing follows on Monday.

title: Entrepreneurs in Zwolle are fed up with loud street evangelists: 'It is getting out of hand'
lead: Zwolle hospitality entrepreneurs have had enough of street evangelists, who make so much noise that people no longer feel like sitting on the terrace. They are sending a letter of complaint to the municipality. "I can understand there is frustration," says evangelist Florens van der Spek in Dit is de Dag, "but the municipality should steer that in the right direction."

title: Exhibition shows how the former owners of Huis Willet-Hothuysen were up to their necks in the slave trade

Restocking shelves

title: The vagus nerve is a hype on social media, this is how you take care of your 'vagus balance' according to doctors
lead: You scroll through Instagram for a moment and before you know it you are in a kind of 'funnel' full of posts about the vagus nerve. It seems as if this nerve is the key to all our health problems. But what does this longest nerve of our system actually do exactly, and how can we look after it? A neurologist and a cardiologist separate the sense from the nonsense.

title: Court case needed to settle escalated neighbour dispute involving Connie Witteman's daughter
lead: The neighbour dispute in Slootdorp, North Holland, in which Constanza Breukhoven, daughter of Connie Witteman, has become embroiled, is not over yet. The matter, which grew stranger and stranger at the end of last year and the beginning of this year, must be settled through a substantive court proceeding.

title: A bra worth 50 million dollars steals the show at the Victoria's Secret Fashion Show
lead: World-famous models, major artists, bigger wings and eye-catching lingerie: everything passed by during the Victoria's Secret Fashion Show on the night of Sunday to Monday. Gigi Hadid shone with glitter wings, Kylie Jenner made her debut in a bra worth at least 50 million dollars, and Dutch top model Doutzen Kroes was also seen on the catwalk.

title: Is your staff discount disappearing? Perk from boss at risk due to tax rules
lead: If it is up to <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity>, from next year employers will no longer be able to simply give their staff a tax-free discount on their own products, such as clothing or subscriptions. An 'enormously appreciated' employment condition threatens to disappear as a result, businesses fear.

title: AD Football Podcast | 'Feyenoord survived a nail-biting Telstar, but they do win it'
lead: Feyenoord saw the gap with the chasers grow this weekend. Van Bronckhorst's side won 3-4 at Telstar themselves, while AZ drew at Cambuur and PSV lost to ADO Den Haag. Ajax also benefited from a big win over FC Groningen.

title: 19 injured in accident with bus and train at entrance to Channel Tunnel
lead: On the French side of the Channel Tunnel to the United Kingdom, a minibus carrying truck drivers and a freight train collided. As far as is known, nineteen people were injured in the accident, including the driver.

title: Municipality of Woerden under fire over AI photos for Koeiemart
lead: The municipality of Woerden is coming under criticism in the AD for using AI-generated images to promote the annual Koeiemart. According to critics, the artificial images detract from the character of the event and from the work of professional photographers.

title: British government bans pornography depicting strangulation or incest
lead: The British government has adopted a law banning pornographic material involving strangulation or incestuous relationships. The reason is an evaluation showing that such images have contributed to the normalisation of those practices among young people.

title: 'Freedom of religion' leads to privileges for believers
lead: Freedom of religion seems a great good. A political and legal achievement whose importance is often underlined. This is what <entity id="person:silvio-erkens">Silvio Erkens</entity> noticed this month. The VVD state secretary of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-landbouw-visserij-voedselzekerheid-en-natuur">Landbouw, Visserij, Voedselzekerheid en Natuur</entity> showed on television and in <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> sympathy for the initiative of the Partij voor de Dieren to put an end to unstunned ritual slaughter.

title: Does Albert Heijn have to stockpile?
lead: In the aftermath of the hacking attempt at Albert Heijn, the call for building extra food reserves was heard again. We make a rough estimate of the financial consequences if the supermarket has to pay for that.

title: Prosecution demands community service and prison sentence against Samer A. (37) for hitting spectators with a plank at pro-Palestinian protest at UvA
Spain fined over Islamophobic chants during friendly match
lead: World football body FIFA has fined the Spanish football federation RFEF 20,000 dollars (just over 17,000 euros) over Islamophobic chants during a Spain practice match against Egypt (0-0) last March. Also, at least 15 percent of the stands must remain empty at the next friendly match.

title: Opposition takes aim at tax plan: no support for 'sneaky freedom contribution'
lead: <entity id="org:kabinet">Het kabinet</entity> will have to amend the tax plan considerably if it wants to be able to count on sufficient support in parliament. Left-wing and right-wing opposition parties are turning against the 'freedom contribution'. This tax increase, which mainly falls on citizens, is meant to yield billions.

title: Hundreds of thousands of French and Italians take to the streets for a better life, but it ends in looting and arson
lead: A day of protest in France on Saturday again ended in large-scale violence with looting, vandalism and arson. It is the work of 'thousands of far-left rioters', said the French minister of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-biza">Binnenlandse Zaken</entity>. 1800 people were arrested and 500 emergency workers were injured. Demonstrations in Italian cities also got out of hand.

title: Medusa meets the mafia: Niccolò Ammaniti does something surprisingly original with the well-known myth
Video | Residents of Saint Petersburg see thick smoke clouds after drone attack
'Fentanyl is so deadly that you cannot do it safely': Teun Voeten on the fentanyl epidemic
lead: In the United States, the fentanyl epidemic has already claimed more than hundreds of thousands of lives. Cultural anthropologist and photographer Teun Voeten saw how the powerful painkiller grew into a devastating street drug. In his book Fentanyl: Hoe een zware pijnstiller in handen viel van nietsontziende drugskartels he describes how the drug trade responded to it. In Nieuwsweekend he talks about the consequences of the epidemic and his criticism of drug policy.

title: 'Body of missing Hajar (29) left in suitcase', no suspect arrested yet
lead: No suspect has yet been arrested for the death of 29-year-old Hajar from Amsterdam, the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> reports. The woman's body was found in the water at the Amsteldijk yesterday morning. She had not been seen since 4 October.

title: More litter on the streets? No, says litter expert, that just seems so: 'We no longer know what it used to be like'
The end of NSC? Party board steps down during congress with appearance by Mona Keijzer
lead: An NSC congress took place in Breda earlier today. The party was founded by Pieter Omtzigt, but has had no party leader since the beginning of this year. The appearance of House of Representatives member Mona Keijzer as guest speaker caused an uproar, after which a large number of NSC members left the hall. In Goed Ingelichte Kring, Patrick Lodiers discusses the incident with AD columnist Angela de Jong and political commentator Tom Staal. He also speaks with NOS political reporter Nouschka van der Meijden, who was present at the congress.

title: Renewed uncertainty about health budget: chronically ill Niels remains uncertain for longer
lead: In recent months unrest over the care plans of <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> has grown, partly due to the abolition of the care costs deduction. Today the minister announced that these plans will be revised. As a result, the future of the health budget remains unclear.

title: Websites taken offline as a precaution: widely used programming language vulnerable to hacking
lead: Websites around the world that use the programming language PHP have been urgently advised to go offline as a precaution because of vulnerabilities. Roughly 70 percent of websites worldwide run on PHP. In the Netherlands, a government website service has already been taken offline.

title: Dutch man suspected of attempted manslaughter after driving into Belgian police officers
lead: A 24-year-old Dutchman was arrested in Belgium after he allegedly tried to drive his van into two police officers, according to the judicial authorities. One of the officers then shot a tyre of the van flat. The man is now in custody and is suspected of attempted manslaughter.

title: Images from Paris quickly spread to Milan this weekend, where young people mobilised via TikTok and looted shops
lead: In Italy too, police had to act this past weekend against often very young vandals, who looted shops and caused damage in Milan. Elsewhere in Italy, such as in Genoa and Calabria, workers and truck drivers are protesting without violence.

title: Also give all adoptees insight into their adoption file without delay

Review of Wicker: wouldn't that madness fit better in a musical?

Expectations of a Fed rate hike are all over the place
lead: Uncertainty about the policy of the American system of central banks is high. A rate hike in October seems unlikely, yet last week the chance suddenly stood at 50%.

title: False start for Ajax in group stage of Conference League
lead: Ajax has made a poor start to the Conference League. The team of Spanish coach Míchel Sánchez suffered a 2-1 defeat in a match interrupted by fireworks against Hajduk Split. Ajax are therefore still without points in the group stage of the not very prestigious European tournament.

title: His mother runs a pub. Yet GGZ therapist Caspar Lehnen advocates an alcohol-free lifestyle
'Illegal use of Schiphol for years': environmental movement and residents take cabinet plans to court
Suspect in killing of Hajar assaulted foster father just before arrest
lead: The 23-year-old Somali Abdi, who is suspected of killing Hajar, was arrested Tuesday morning at the home of his foster father. This happened after he had assaulted his foster father.

title: Abdul El-Sayed is the favorite enemy of the right in America
Schools surrounded by snack bars and other fast food: municipalities want to intervene
lead: A new snack bar, grill room or ice cream parlour around the corner from a school? Municipalities want to be able to put a stop to that more often in future. New research in ten cities shows that nearly 94 percent of secondary schools and mbo schools are surrounded by a high volume of unhealthy food options. Not a single school examined is located in a healthy environment.

title: Four dead and nearly forty injured after fire at Canadian military base

Joling only made his decision known to his colleagues last week. According to insiders, Tino Martin and Mart Hoogkamer will be added to the Toppers in the short term.

title: The gold wine glasses in Love is Blind are mainly very handy for the TV maker
lead: There are more gold wine glasses to be spotted in Love is Blind: Nederland than there are successful couples emerging. Why do all the candidates actually drink from these glasses? There is a specific reason for that.

title: Politie doet onderzoek in pand in Amsterdam waar 29-jarige vrouw waarschijnlijk is gedood
lead: De politie doet een uitgebreid onderzoek in een pand aan De Klencke in Buitenveldert, Amsterdam-Zuid, in verband met het overlijden van de 29-jarige Hajar.

title: Environmental movement and residents take the cabinet's Schiphol plans to court
lead: A broad coalition of environmental groups and residents' groups is going to the <entity id="org:raad-van-state">Raad van State</entity> to challenge the new rules for Schiphol that the cabinet introduces on 1 November. According to them, this legitimises "years of illegal use of Schiphol". The group wants to still force a substantial reduction in the number of flights.

title: Explainer | Why this Democrat deliberately runs a 'hopeless' race
New priorities for infrastructure: these are the biggest winners and losers of the cabinet's choices
Mother contacted care workers shortly before death of Julie (15): 'We can't do anything about that either, that is always the answer'
lead: 'My greatest concern is the safety of my child. I want to prevent something serious from having to happen before action is actually taken.' More than a month after a distraught mother sent this cry for help in an email to care agencies, her 15-year-old daughter Julie died in a shelter in Groningen.

title: Journalist Paul Vugts on corrupt Amsterdam official Jim B.
In a desperate attempt to exclude the non-Western newcomer, the populist flank is destroying its own traditions
lead: Reactionary forces keep pushing the country into a deadlock, argues Shervin Nekuee. Just look at the motion on scrapping iftar network celebrations by the <entity id="org:politie">Nationale Politie</entity>.

title: One of the blackest days in French history: will Emmanuel Macron cross the finish line?
End of net metering scheme in 2027: solar power for hot water can be smart
lead: If the net metering scheme for solar panels ends on 1 January 2027, it is no longer as advantageous to feed surplus solar power back into the grid. It is therefore recommended to use more of the electricity directly yourself or store it. This can be done by charging an electric car with it or installing a home battery to […]

title: Residents of Amsterdam arrested in investigation into violence in Overasselt, weapons also found
lead: The <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> arrested three new suspects on Monday, two of whom are directly linked to the violence in the Gelderland village of Overasselt earlier this month. They are men aged 24 and 25 from Amsterdam.

Team spirit drives historic World Cup performance by Dutch gymnasts: 'Also play FIFA together'
lead: On Tuesday evening, in the orange-coloured Ahoy of all places, the Dutch gymnasts delivered the best World Cup performance ever in a team final. The strength of the team lies in its strong team spirit. "We can say anything to each other."

title: Zelensky seeks support in Brussels after Russian attacks and criticism from Trump
lead: Ukraine is under heavy pressure from Russian attacks and criticism from US President Trump. President Zelensky is therefore in Brussels seeking support from European leaders. According to the politicians present, it is important to show precisely now that Europe stands behind Ukraine.

title: EU designates 4 Dutch projects as strategic for critical raw materials
Max Porter's successful novella yields powerful and boundary-crossing theatre
lead: In Shy, the stage adaptation of the book of the same name by Max Porter, you are mercilessly put on the spot as a spectator. Actor and theatre maker Romijn Scholten makes you feel responsible as an audience member for the fate of his character.

title: New setback for housing development in Amsterdam-Noord: House of Representatives backs keeping shipyard Damen
Amsterdam has more and more 'power couples': they not only have more money, but also more stable relationships
AP takes the next step in AI oversight
lead: The Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens (AP) is further preparing for oversight of artificial intelligence (AI). With the launch of the new directorate Toezicht en Coördinatie AI/Algoritmes (TCA), the task structure is taking increasingly concrete shape. The new directorate continues the coordinating oversight of AI and algorithms that the AP has been carrying out since 2023. In addition, TCA is preparing AI market oversight and, together with the <entity id="org:rijksinspectie-digitale-infrastructuur">Rijksinspectie Digitale Infrastructuur</entity> (RDI), is shaping the 'AI sandbox' and the joint AI Coordination Centre.

title: These parents home-school: 'This should be different, we thought when we had children'
lead: For some families it is the most normal thing in the world: their children do not go to school, but learn at home. At the kitchen table, in the forest or on the trampoline. But that freedom is under pressure. <entity id="org:kabinet">Het kabinet</entity> wants to restrict home education.

title: Those who grow up on welfare more often receive benefits themselves later or earn less
lead: Young people who grow up in a household on welfare also have a less favourable position on the labour market as adults. They less often have work, earn a lower hourly wage and more often receive a benefit themselves. This is shown by new research from the <entity id="org:zbo-centraal-bureau-voor-de-statistiek">Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek</entity> (CBS).

title: Van Borst's view: 'A coach who speaks neither Dutch nor English is unfit for the Eredivisie'
lead: Ajax surprisingly lost last Thursday in the Europa League to Croatian side Hajduk Split (2-1). A setback for the Amsterdam club, because things are not going well in the Eredivisie either. With 15 points from 8 matches, Ajax is fifth in the competition and has more reason to look down than up. "The gap is considerable", says Hugo Borst in his statement of the week.

title: Court: further investigation needed at three pig farmers into cutting and burning off pig tails
lead: Pigs in Need Foundation asked the state secretary for Agriculture to conduct an investigation and possibly intervene at three pig farmers whom the foundation says unlawfully dock the tails of their animals. According to the state secretary, it is not possible to enforce the ban. The Board of Appeal ruled differently on Tuesday.

title: State Secretary Eerenberg: limit for overly heavy taxation of labour is coming into sight
lead: "We have to be careful not to tax labour too heavily." That is what <entity id="pos:staatssecretaris-van-financien">staatssecretaris van Financiën</entity> Eelco Eerenberg says in the weekly conversation on RTL Z. According to him, the limit is now coming into sight.

title: Mayor is fed up with nuisance in Hoogeveen: 'Parents, take your responsibility'
lead: The Drenthe town of Hoogeveen has for days been plagued by nuisance from young people. They intimidate passersby and throw fireworks at people. Mayor <entity id="person:martijn-breukelman">Martijn Breukelman</entity> is fed up and calls on parents to take action.

title: Anyone who simply gives up on non-voters should not then complain about low turnout
lead: In my view we should aim for a much higher turnout

title: Getting fit before an operation makes sense. "Patients said: I am really doing something, not just worrying"
lead: Those who go into an operation fitter have a lower chance of complications. That sounds logical, but it has barely been demonstrated. Joëlle Dhanis did just that for gynaecological cancers. "At the Radboudumc in Nijmegen, this has already been introduced as standard."

title: The never-ending soap opera of the cabinet over gambling ads
lead: The political chaos surrounding the self-created problem of online gambling ads keeps going. A motion for a total ban on gambling ads was defeated. Meanwhile, we saw how things went in the gambling capital of the world, Las Vegas.

title: Shell and Exxon treat themselves to 1.4 billion from NAM's coffers, minister demands explanation
lead: Oil giants Shell and Exxon Mobil have treated themselves to a hefty bonus. At their request, subsidiary NAM paid out an extra dividend of as much as 1.36 billion euros. The payout breaches agreements made with the state. <entity id="person:pieter-heerma">Minister Heerma</entity> will ask for clarification about how this came about.

title: Pope Leo is missing part of a lung, but smiles broadly and can simply travel to South America
Overasselt suspect Jan G. transferred to prison in the Netherlands
lead: The 28-year-old Jan G. from Overasselt is back on Dutch soil. He spent almost a month in a prison in Germany, but was extradited today. He is suspected of involvement in an attempt to import nearly 4,000 kilos of cocaine.

title: Gymnastics coach of Simone Biles and the Dutch team: 'There is a culture shift underway in the gymnastics world, but fundamentally a lot is still wrong'
lead: Aimee Boorman coached Simone Biles for years and was brought in as coach of the Dutch team in 2021, just when gymnastics was in a deep crisis due to reports of boundary-crossing behaviour. Now she is back in the Netherlands for the gymnastics World Championships in Rotterdam. "I care little about medals, success is a happy gymnast."

title: 340.000 homes in ten years: the impact of migration on the housing market
lead: For years, demographer Jan van de Beek warned about the major impact of migration on the Dutch housing market. But his message received little attention. New research from the Economisch Instituut voor de Bouw (EIB) shows that between 2015 and 2024 migration was responsible for approximately 60 percent of the additional housing demand. If the current trend continues, around 340.000 homes will be needed over the next ten years as a result of migration.

title: New rules for zoos: 'Our duty to ensure that an animal really feels good'
lead: The licensing system for zoos is going to be overhauled. According to <entity id="person:silvio-erkens">staatssecretaris Erkens</entity>, the current rules stand in the way of improvements in animal welfare. "Not every park needs to have a herd of elephants."

title: US Election Update | Winning votes proves quite difficult in crucial Maine
lead: Until the US midterm elections on 3 November, NU.nl will keep you updated weekly on the latest developments. Today: on the campaign trail in Maine.

title: Chaos on Belgian motorway: man threatens to blow up vehicle with explosives
lead: A stretch of motorway south of Liège has been closed because a motorist stopped his vehicle and threatens to blow it up with explosives. According to the public prosecutor, the man is armed and traces of explosives have been found.

title: Deputy sounds alarm over growing shortage of social rental homes
lead: Although nearly half of South Hollanders are income-eligible for a social rental home, the province has proportionally fewer and fewer such homes. In 2020, 29 percent of all homes in <entity id="org:provincie-zuid-holland">Zuid-Holland</entity> were social rentals; according to the latest figures that is 28.1 percent. Deputy Anne Koning (housing, PRO) therefore sounds the alarm.

title: If the relationship between Heinen and Jetten is not good, it becomes difficult for the cabinet
lead: The cooperation between prime minister <entity id="person:rob-jetten">Rob Jetten</entity> (D66) and <entity id="pos:minister-van-financien">minister van Financiën</entity> <entity id="person:eelco-heinen">Eelco Heinen</entity> (VVD) does not always run smoothly. Yet the prime minister and his finance minister must be a strong duo to bring a cabinet to a successful conclusion, experienced experts know. Now that the two are holding talks with opposition parties, it will become clear how solid the duo is.

title: Owner of China daycare sentenced to life for poisoning more than 200 children
lead: The owner of a Chinese daycare centre and five of her employees have been sentenced to prison terms for poisoning more than two hundred children with non-edible paint. The owner has been given a life sentence.

title: Soldiers and harsher penalties: Italy tightens law after looting in Milan
lead: The Italian government has adopted a new security law against rioters. According to Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni, the police can thereby act more strictly during major disturbances, such as last weekend in Milan. There, demonstrations turned into riots in which shops were vandalised and looted. The government wants in this way to prevent further disturbances like those in France.

title: State Secretary Tielen: 'If schools say they have no interest in a phone ban, then I think: come on, guys'
Asylum seekers are being dragged around in Ter Apel. Onto the bus, briefly to bed, back onto the bus, and then again tomorrow
This is the best almond speculaas, but why does it have a little windmill on it?
lead: Baker Kees van der Woerd bakes the best almond speculaas cookie in the Netherlands. But why is the cookie actually called that?

title: A hundred magical moon prints by Yoshitoshi: a source of inspiration for Vincent van Gogh
lead: The Van Gogh Museum received the beautiful complete Japanese print series 'One Hundred Aspects of the Moon' by Yoshitoshi from an estate and is now showing it.

title: Prosecution demands prison sentences for serious assault on boy in Beverwijk
lead: The <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> has demanded prison sentences of up to two years on Thursday against three young people for attempted manslaughter. They are suspected of seriously assaulting a seventeen-year-old boy in Beverwijk last year. The violence was filmed and spread online.

title: Russian businessman successfully enters Dutch film distribution market, but conceals it via Cyprus
lead: Film distribution is risky business. Every year distributors disappear in the Netherlands and new ones arrive. But how quickly and effectively newcomer 18K Film is making its way surprises many. Who is this newcomer? And how does 18K Film get its money?

title: Growth in central government employment slows
lead: Central government employment grew in 2025 in ten provinces, while it fell in two provinces: in <entity id="org:gemeente-groningen">Groningen</entity> by 0.3 percent and in <entity id="org:provincie-flevoland">Flevoland</entity> by 2.5 percent. Two thirds of the growth took place in the three Randstad provinces (7,067 fte), with an emphasis on <entity id="org:provincie-zuid-holland">Zuid-Holland</entity>. That is a lower share than a year earlier, when 80 percent of the growth in those provinces took place. In absolute terms there was also less growth in the Randstad.

title: Oldebroek nevertheless raises the rainbow flag, with the mayor present. 'It is an opportunity to make a connection'
Jeroen van der Boom learned of Gerard Joling's departure from De Toppers through the media
lead: Jeroen van der Boom did not know about Gerard Joling's departure from De Toppers until it was announced in the media. "Just like for many, the news came as a big surprise", Van der Boom writes on Instagram.

title: Techno legend Richie Hawtin to give free ADE performance on Leidseplein on Thursday
Nurlaila Karim moved in with her mother (81) as a carer: 'Suddenly you slip back into those old patterns'
lead: Not long ago she was too scared to drive in the dark. In recent years musical star Nurlaila Karim, now appearing in Cats, has been shooting down all the bears on the road, she tells weekend magazine Mezza.

title: Planned strike in regional transport will not go ahead: talks on new collective labour agreement resumed
lead: The planned strike in regional transport on Thursday will not go ahead. Trade unions and employers are resuming talks on a new collective labour agreement. FNV has therefore suspended the actions for two weeks, in the hope of still reaching an agreement.

title: Cabinet presents strategy to protect children online
Some northern municipalities lost dozens of bus stops in recent years
lead: Over the past six years more than 1100 bus stops have disappeared in the Netherlands. Especially in <entity id="org:provincie-drenthe">Drenthe</entity> and <entity id="org:gemeente-groningen">Groningen</entity> the supply decreased: both provinces have lost more than 13 percent of their stops since 2020.

title: Suspect in murder of pregnant woman escapes death penalty after fleeing to Italy
lead: American Lee Gilley (39) is suspected of murdering his pregnant wife Christa Bauer Gilley (38), cutting his ankle monitor and fleeing to Italy. After months of negotiations with the United States, Italy permits partial extradition, Fox News reports.

title: Floor Jansen leaves Finnish metal band Nightwish after thirteen years: 'This decision is necessary'
lead: Singer Floor Jansen (45) is leaving the well-known Finnish metal band Nightwish after thirteen years, with which she had great international success. She speaks of a difficult decision that was made jointly.

title: Many figures after the decimal point: this is behind those strange prices at the pump
lead: The fuel prices are clearly displayed at petrol stations on large screens. But such a price contains many figures after the decimal point. Why is that, asks reader Mario van der Linden. Our car expert Niek Schenk provides an answer.

title: How the super seed of Ragnild's father turned her life upside down
lead: Ragnild (52) is not a donor child, but discovered that she does have a donor father: in the 1980s he donated his sperm dozens of times. "When I found that out, I really thought I was going crazy. Anyone could be my brother or sister."

title: The unusual love story of Bart, Trees and Ada: 'We never wanted to cause offense'
lead: Ada is married to Bart and has a 6-year-old son when she falls in love with Trees. That spark ignites in 1978. Until Bart's death in 2012, the three live under one roof. Now Ada (86) and Trees (80) live in their first shared home. "We never wanted to cause offense."

title: Regular deliveries to Albert Heijn supermarkets fully resumed: shelves are getting fuller again
lead: Albert Heijn has fully resumed deliveries of ambient and fresh products to stores across the country. On Thursday morning, empty shelves, mainly of fresh products, could still be seen at various Albert Heijn branches. Online ordering is still not possible, and the supermarket chain's website is also still unreachable. We will keep you informed of the latest developments in this liveblog.

title: Mess
lead: Democracy falls in the American autumn

title: 24,5 degrees: warmest 30 September since 1901
lead: The mercury rose this afternoon at the <entity id="org:koninklijk-nederlands-meteorologisch-instituut">KNMI</entity> in De Bilt to 24,5 degrees. That makes it now also officially the warmest 30 September since 1901. The old date record was 24,3 degrees in 1975.

title: Not in my backyard. Suddenly the arrival of data centres in American towns is shaping the elections
lead: Anger at Big Tech, fear of job losses and existential AI anxiety are fuelling American resistance to data centres. Opposition to the data centres has grown into "the most cross-party issue since beer".

title: Mega fine of 25 billion dollars for Meta for misleading users
lead: A judge in the US state of New Mexico has imposed a fine of 25 billion dollars, roughly 22.3 billion euros, on social media company Meta for misleading Facebook users about their privacy.

title: Opinion by the children's ombudsman: 'Children who play football deserve more protection against racism and discrimination'

lead: Het kabinet heeft beloofd een deel van zijn nieuwe belastingplan voor spaargeld en beleggingen te herschrijven, slechts twee dagen nadat...

title: French looters selling goods on Vinted: 'Handling stolen goods is punishable'
lead: Want to buy items via Vinted? Make sure they do not come from looted shops in France. If you do buy these items, you are liable to prosecution. The trading platform says it has taken 'immediate' action to detect and remove suspicious listings.

title: Former mayor Koen Schuiling sentenced again on appeal for masturbating in public
lead: The police court sentenced Koen Schuiling in March 2025 for masturbating in his car. On appeal, the former <entity id="pos:burgemeester-groningen">burgemeester van Groningen</entity> asked for acquittal. The court does not believe his defence and again finds that there is enough evidence to impose a fine of 250 euros.

title: Heineken must pay 111 million euro in damages to Greek competitor that the company obstructed for years
Unions threaten: one day per week strike in regional transport
lead: If you sometimes travel by regional bus, you may face strikes in the coming months. Unions FNV and CNV are threatening this. The unions and employers have not yet reached agreement on a new collective labour agreement.

title: Houthi missiles hit Yemen's presidential palace for the first time: five dead
lead: Houthi rebels in Yemen carried out a missile attack on the presidential Al-Maashiq palace in Aden, which serves as the headquarters of the internationally recognised government of Yemen.

title: A PostcodeKanjer for Carrie ten Napel and the only talk show that doesn't cynically laugh off positivity
House of Representatives raises the rainbow flag for the first time to support LGBTI people worldwide
A culture of fear is the most normal thing in the world, both in top sport and in an open-plan office
House of Representatives wants to tackle paper gifts to spare 'small' savers
lead: A majority of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> wants to partly fund the reform of box 3 by tackling paper gifts. That is a tax-favourable way to give money and pay less inheritance tax. Last week <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> still wanted to pay for the reform by taxing just over 800,000 extra savers and investors. But that plan is not going ahead.

title: How Israel terrorises, breaks and leaves Palestinian teenage boys to waste away behind bars
ME deployed again in Floradorp, five arrests, including four teenagers: officers pelted with stones, fire set and barriers placed on the road
Aid worker infected with Ebola discharged from hospital after negative test
lead: The Ebola-infected aid worker of Doctors Without Borders (AzG) has been discharged from the hospital, <entity id="org:rijksinstituut-voor-volksgezondheid-en-milieu">RIVM</entity> reports. The patient was repatriated last week from the Democratic Republic of Congo to the Netherlands and was treated at the Leiden University Medical Center.

title: Polish parliament approves relaxed abortion law, president can block it
lead: The Polish parliament has agreed to relax abortion legislation. Assisting in carrying out an abortion will as a result no longer be punishable. The conservative-nationalist president Karol Nawrocki can however still block the amendment.

title: ADE director never dances at his own party
lead: More than half a million visitors and over twelve hundred events. Led by Jan-Willem van de Ven, the Amsterdam Dance Event starts on Wednesday. 'Sometimes I even tell him to enjoy himself.'

title: Curfew in French cities to curb new violence
lead: While shopkeepers and entrepreneurs are still assessing the damage from the riots and looting of last weekend, new demonstrations are already on the agenda.

title: School trips would be better off going to data centers and nuclear power plants
lead: In What Will My Children Do Later? economist Daniel Susskind explores work in a future with AI. He offers no certainty about types of jobs or required skills. Learning to deal with artificial intelligence: that is what matters. And, he says, you no longer choose a profession, but a field that interests you.

title: An appendix for managers
lead: Uh, no, we are not going to talk about the boss's appendix today. An appendix is indeed that worm-shaped appendage in the lower right of the abdomen, which can become inflamed in an annoying way and cause considerable pain. But it is also an appendix to a book. And that is exactly what I happen to be working on.

title: How Albert Heijn's crisis week unfolded, a chain that feared 'framing'
lead: For Albert Heijn it was a crisis week. Due to a 'cybersecurity incident', shelves were empty and groceries still cannot be delivered. Crisis communication is part of such an emergency. The supermarket chain tried to stay in control, was not generous with information and feared 'framing'.

title: Devambez shows how to keep the rebellious people under control
More Room for New Schools
lead: Suppose you want to found a school. Then you hardly need to do more than collect signatures. Those signatures come from parents who are interested in the new school, without any guarantee that they will enrol their child(ren) there later. Next, you submit an application to the ministry of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-onderwijs-cultuur-en-wetenschap">OCW</entity>: this is our plan, this is the neighbourhood we have in mind, and here are the signatures. If the minister then approves the initiative, which almost always happens, the law Meer… determines…

title: Shadowy battle over Russian oil giant Lukoil runs through the White House
Verstappen condemns online hate against teammate after penalty in race
lead: Max Verstappen has condemned the online hate against his teammate Chris Lulham after the GT World Challenge race in Portimão. The British driver received a penalty on Saturday during his performance, which set the team back far. Verstappen then still drove from 24th to 9th place during his closing stint.

title: House of Representatives wants 150,000 citizens to be deployable in crises and disasters
lead: If a major crisis breaks out and <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity>, the army and emergency services can no longer cope, citizens must step in to ensure society keeps running. Especially in the first three days, these so-called civilian reserves can help prevent chaos from arising. The House of Representatives wants their number to be quickly expanded to 150,000 by 2030.

title: Rubio urges Israel to act firmly against settlers after 'disturbing images'
lead: The US wants Israel to do more to prevent attacks by settlers on the occupied West Bank. "We are very concerned by those images and what we see," says Foreign Minister Marco Rubio. "We have asked the Israelis - and continue to ask them - to act firmly against this kind of thing." Follow all developments in the Middle East in our liveblog.

title: From supple teens to powerful thirtysomethings: the evolution of gymnastics
lead: This coming Saturday Rotterdam will host the World Gymnastics Championships for the third time. Since the first edition in 1987, women's gymnastics has changed considerably. Where the gymnasts back then were on average not yet 17 years old, and one of the winners in Rotterdam was only 14, that average is now over 20. How did that change come about?

title: Another climate record: the amount of water vapour in the atmosphere
lead: That records keep falling in a warming climate is no surprise. We regularly see them in the news about, for example, high temperatures, low water levels or a possibly record-breaking El Niño. There are also records that get less attention. Climate scientist Andrew Dessler recently wrote about one such record on his blog The Climate Brink: the […] Read more posts on Sargasso

title: Politicians use ChatGPT on a large scale during debates, but how bad is that? 'There is still a taboo'
Hakim had 6 shells, 10 supercobras and 19 kilos of fireworks in his home
lead: Six shells, ten supercobras, a homemade Pringles projectile and 19 kilos of consumer fireworks. All of it is in Hakim's home when the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> raids his house.

title: Van Bronckhorst wants Feyenoord to play with bravado in Seville
lead: Coach Giovanni van Bronckhorst wants Feyenoord to play with bravado in the away match against Real Betis as well. "We have to show courage and also dare to play football ourselves," he said at a press conference in the stadium of the Seville club.

title: Lower House wants large network of civilian reservists for local crisis response
lead: The Netherlands must have 130,000 generally trained civilian reservists by 2030. In addition, specialised reservists must become available in the fields of technology, logistics and security. The <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">Tweede Kamer</entity> has agreed to two motions by CDA Member of Parliament Maes van Lanschot that are meant to make this possible.

title: Trumps Barbertje heet Volodymyr Zelensky
lead: Trump maakt Zelensky tot zondebok voor zijn eigen falende beleid en hij gokt erop dat de Maga-kiezer hem gelooft, schrijft columnist Bernard Hammelburg.

title: Marcouch: democracy weakens when government lets citizens get stuck
lead: Protecting the democratic constitutional state requires long-term investment in housing, education, care and an accessible government. As long as citizens get stuck and experience no improvement, democratic procedures lose credibility. The Arnhem mayor <entity id="person:ahmed-marcouch">Ahmed Marcouch</entity> warned of this on Tuesday during the first Nationale Democratielezing in Nieuwspoort.

title: Marathon Amsterdam zorgt zondag voor grote wegafsluitingen, meer dan 30.000 deelnemers verwacht
lead: Dit jaar nemen meer dan 30.000 mensen deel aan de Amsterdam Marathon.

title: Visually impaired Femke (25) found a job after many rejections: 'Thinking in solutions, not in problems'
lead: Femke was born with a rare eye condition. But limited? She absolutely doesn't feel that way. Finding work is not a given for visually impaired people, but after many applications she succeeded. "Sometimes I'm faster than my colleagues."

title: Dakar Rally wants to avoid Saudi Arabia and move to Africa: 'Fine, just make a decision'
lead: Officially nothing has been communicated yet, but organiser ASO has already informed the participating Dakar Rally teams about an alternative route far from Saudi Arabia, where tensions still persist. A return to Africa seems imminent.

title: Youths cause damage at asylum centre protest in Rhenen
lead: Damage was caused at an asylum centre protest in Rhenen. 400 youths gathered while the town hall was meeting about the reception of asylum seekers.

title: This is why you get car sick faster in an electric car
lead: More and more electric cars are on our roads. And with that increase a new phenomenon has also emerged. People namely get car sick faster in an electric car than in a petrol or diesel car. According to <entity id="org:zbo-nederlandse-organisatie-voor-toegepast-natuurwetenschappelijk-onderzoek">TNO</entity>, around sixty percent of people get car sick in an electric car. What can you do about that car sickness? Tech editor at Tweakers Arnoud Wokke explains it in the Villa.

title: Wierd Duk brought down with one simple question
lead: Roderik van Grieken: 'In effect he lets Duk himself explain how inconsistent his reasoning is'

title: Gerard has been fighting for a safe road in his village for 30 years, but money from The Hague is uncertain again
lead: For more than thirty years Gerard Nij Bijvank has been fighting for a bypass near Mariënheem. The N35, the most unsafe national road in our country, runs right through the village. The budget to tackle the road is there. But politics in The Hague may withdraw it. Again.

title: France and Germany present plan to prop up car sector; climate takes a back seat
Opinion: Categorising people is not the right path to inclusion
Number of people experiencing discrimination in Amsterdam rises slightly
Minister Yeşilgöz calls Russia 'our enemy', Russian embassy demands clarification
lead: The Russian embassy in the Netherlands wants clarification about the remark by defence minister Dilan Yeşilgöz that Russia is 'our enemy'. The VVD leader said that during the debate on the defence budget in <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity>.

title: Katwijk council wants to agree to construction of medicine factory
lead: A majority of the Katwijk municipal council plans to agree next week to the arrival of the American pharmaceutical company Eli Lilly. During a committee meeting it emerged that most parties want to grant Eli Lilly a permit for the construction of a large factory worth 3 billion dollars (around 2.6 billion euros). The company wants to make diabetes and weight-loss pills there.

lead: The number of abortions in the Netherlands rose slightly in 2025. Healthcare providers performed almost 40,000 terminations of pregnancy, an increase of 1.25 percent compared with 2024. lead: The phasing out of closed youth care is the subject of a debate in <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> this week. The Vereniging Nederlandse Gemeenten (VNG) earlier apologised on behalf of municipalities for the abuses within closed youth care and says it supports the phasing out. The VNG is giving three points of attention for the House debate of 30 September.

title: Feyenoord flop Casper Tengstedt comes alive in France: 'He is very talented and has many qualities'
lead: Casper Tengstedt disappointed as a multimillion-euro signing for Feyenoord and left last summer after only one year. The French club Toulouse picked him up. There he is one of the standouts.

title: Chief economist at BNP Paribas: the French themselves also see that something needs to be done
lead: Is a new European debt crisis coming? France is the problem child. Isabelle Mateos y Lago, chief economist at BNP Paribas, is not among the pessimists. 'The problem is solvable.'

title: 'Musk himself switched off satellite internet for Ukraine with Trump's permission'
lead: Elon Musk himself approached Trump with the proposal to restrict satellite internet in Ukraine, which undermined the country's air defence. That is what the newspaper The Telegraph , which bases itself on anonymous sources, writes. Follow all developments in the war in Ukraine in our liveblog.

title: Loyal Trump friend and envoy Paolo Zampolli allowed himself some political liberties that went slightly too far
Round the world
lead: 'I watch a lot of videos by, what's his name again, Andrew Tate.' My eleven-year-old son says it casually while playing football on the street with his sister. 'Do you know him?' he adds when he sees my worried face. I am about to start a parental lecture, but then they can't hold it in any longer. My children burst out laughing at the same time. Always fun to drive mom up the wall.

title: Many pupils in practical education live in poverty. 'And then the internship falls apart, because that boy has to share one bike with his little brother'
lead: At least half of the pupils at practical education schools grow up in relative poverty. Some cannot pay for their school supplies. The Jeugdeducatiefonds can pay for work shoes, aprons or bicycles for them. The same applies at De Bolster in Groningen. "With this money you can immediately fix what is standing in the way of their functioning at school."

title: Trump reverses tariffs and sanctions on Russian energy
Frugal member states threaten to veto unless substantial cuts are made to the EU budget
Cabinet wants to link transport services to counter the reduction of public transport in the regions
In Brahms's Klavierstücke, every note sounds like a longing for the next one
Boy (14) escapes from Dutch institution and causes accident in Belgium
lead: In Belgium, a 14-year-old boy from the Netherlands caused a collision. The boy reportedly escaped from an institution in the Netherlands and was driving a van that crashed head-on into an oncoming vehicle. Three people were injured. The teenager was behind the wheel of the van.

title: More than a hundred people arrested after new riots in Paris
lead: During new unrest in Paris, 108 arrests were made on Sunday, the police report. In the first hour of the night from Sunday to Monday, nine more arrests followed. The police speak of "youths with opportunistic, criminal intentions" who are looting shops.

title: Good compliance in zero-emission zones
lead: Compliance with the rules in the zero-emission zones is going well. In the past summer, more than 99 percent of trucks and delivery vans met the access requirements.

title: Dutch gymnasts seventh in World Championship final, gold for Japan
lead: The Dutch gymnasts finished seventh in the team final at the World Championships in Rotterdam. Casimir Schmidt, Elijah Faverus, Amine Abaidi, Loran de Munck and Jermain Grünberg scored 241,294 points.

title: Liverpool wins Virgil van Dijk's anniversary match, Zian Flemming scores for Ipswich against City
lead: Liverpool secured an important win against Brentford. In Virgil van Dijk's 200th match as captain of The Reds, the away side won with difficulty, 1-2. Manchester City also won, despite a counter goal from Zian Flemming.

title: Arwin's little daughter suddenly stopped talking, now as a deaf pastor he is giving his first service in sign language
lead: His vocabulary still needs expanding. He already knows the signs for 'God' and 'peace', but Arwin van Wilgenburg still has to practise hard on the name signs for all kinds of Biblical figures. Furthermore, the man from Hoevelaken is ready for his first service as a deaf pastor, at the end of October. "Sign language is very physical and visual, almost theatre."

title: This is how safe readers find Amsterdam traffic: 'It was always quiet here, but what are those Canta's and Birò's doing on the bike path all of a sudden?'
World Championships gymnastics team final halfway, Netherlands for now in eighth place
lead: After the surprising qualification for the team final on Saturday evening, the Dutch gymnasts take to the floor on Tuesday evening in Ahoy. After three apparatuses, Oranje is in eighth place. Can Casimir Schmidt, Loran de Munck, Elijah Faverus, Amine Abaidi and Jermain Grünberg still work their way up the ranking in the remaining events?

title: Track cyclist Van de Wouw knocked out early in keirin at world championships
lead: Hetty van de Wouw finished the track cycling world championships with just one medal. The triple reigning world champion from last year was knocked out in the quarter-finals of the keirin and therefore only takes home the silver from the kilometre time trial. The 28-year-old from Brabant tried to pass on the outside in her heat, but could not get through and finished last.

title: Trade with Russia remains lucrative, but companies run risks
lead: This week the European Union added nearly sixteen hundred companies and individuals to the sanctions list against Russia. Even so, prohibited goods still reach the country via detours. Companies that cooperate can earn a lot of money, but they are also playing with fire.

title: Colapinto wants fans to stop threats against F1 colleagues: 'It doesn't help me'
lead: Franco Colapinto has called on his fans to stop online hate campaigns against his Formula 1 colleagues. The Argentine makes this call following the threats directed at his teammate Pierre Gasly and Lando Norris.

title: Dutch gymnasts unable to surprise in World Championships team final, gold for Japan in Ahoy
lead: Following their surprising qualification for the team final on Saturday evening, the Dutch gymnasts competed in Ahoy on Tuesday evening. The team of Casimir Schmidt, Loran de Munck, Elijah Faverus, Amine Abaidi and Jermain Grünberg did not manage to produce another surprise. The Netherlands finished seventh, while Japan took the world title.

title: Flight from Tel Aviv to Vienna makes emergency landing after bomb threat
lead: A plane from Tel Aviv to Vienna made an emergency landing in the Bulgarian capital Sofia on Sunday evening. The aircraft diverted due to a bomb threat, a spokesperson for airline Austrian Airlines told news agency Reuters.

title: The Dutch teacher would rather yell himself hoarse than drill his pupils
France is heading towards a toxic cocktail of unrest and political weakness ahead of elections
After a flop at RTL, broadcaster WNL is going to try it: Frank van Leeuwen presents new daily quiz
lead: WNL is launching a daily news quiz on NPO 1 next year. The presenter is Frank van Leeuwen, who, in addition to his work as anchorman of Goedemorgen Nederland, and last summer also Goedenavond Nederland , now has a new job. WNL confirms this to this site.

title: Barça baffled by banner from PSG fans referencing horror film
lead: FC Barcelona has filed a complaint with UEFA about a banner from Paris Saint-Germain supporters. The banner shows the Barça logo edited with a chainsaw. It is a reference to the well-known horror film The Texas Chain Saw Massacre .

title: Tallon Griekspoor advances to quarterfinal in Brussels after win over world number 45
lead: Tallon Griekspoor has reached the quarterfinal of the tennis tournament in Brussels. The 30-year-old from Haarlem beat Mariano Navone, the Argentinian world number 45, in the second round. The score was 7-6 (4) 7-5.

title: Wrong-way driver in fatal A2 accident became unwell while driving
lead: The driver who ended up on the wrong side of the A2 near Breukelen on Saturday and died had, according to the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity>, become unwell while driving. The man then collided with two cars on the other carriageway.

title: Frenkie de Jong returns to FC Barcelona matchday squad
lead: Frenkie de Jong is fit enough to play again. The midfielder has been included in the FC Barcelona matchday squad for Saturday's match against Real Betis. "He is training well and is ready to get minutes," said coach Hansi Flick at a press conference. "He is a top player, very focused. Frenkie gives us more options in midfield."

title: Broad coalition launches petition to block increase in labour tax as tension in The Hague rises
Cabinet wants structural insight into tasks and funds
lead: The cabinet wants to structurally show which tasks municipalities and provinces have and whether they receive enough money for them. That is what minister <entity id="person:pieter-heerma">Pieter Heerma</entity> of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-biza">Binnenlandse Zaken</entity> writes to <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity>. The insight should lead to a better conversation with decentralised governments about tasks and funds.

title: As if house building were not slow enough already, now the interest rate spectre also appears on the building site
Nederland haalt EU-doel voor gasopslag na ingrijpen van de overheid
lead: Staatsbedrijf <entity id="org:zbo-economie-bedrijven-en-nationale-rekeningen">EBN</entity> heeft zijn opdracht voltooid om de Nederlandse ondergrondse gasopslagfaciliteiten te vullen tot 64 procent van de capaciteit, in lijn met het Europese doel.

title: Goldman Sachs buy advice does not help CoreWeave out of the fire either
lead: The share is now worth buying, says the investment bank. The financing costs are not that bad, though.

title: Recognising the state of Palestine: the CDA is still open to it
lead: Will the Netherlands recognise the Palestinian state? That question is back on the table now that relations between the Netherlands and Israel are under further pressure. The CDA advocated recognising Palestine last year, but does it still hold that view? Yes, says Tweede Kamer member Maes van Lanschot, but only under conditions.
