Yesterday Ukrainian President Zelensky announced that the country would no longer abide by this. Zelensky cited the continuing Russian drone attacks as the reason. Shortly afterwards Russia announced that Ukraine had fired on an oil refinery in Ryazan. Trump is far from pleased about all this. Speaking to the American news channel Newsmax, he called it "a disgrace" that Ukraine had resumed attacks on Russian refineries. According to him, this is driving up fuel prices worldwide. Last Friday Trump announced that he had found a solution to this for American consumers. He then announced a deal with Russian President Putin on the supply of Russian diesel to the US. "I think they both really want to see an end to it," Trump says of the war. "But I find it harder to deal with Zelensky than with Putin." White House and Starlink That the relationship between Trump and Zelensky is under serious strain became noticeable for the Ukrainian army in recent days. Suddenly there were major problems with the country's air defence, because the army could only partly use the Starshield network, the military branch of the Starlink satellite network. Ukrainian drones could not fly faster than 160 kilometres per hour because of an unstable connection. The news agency Reuters reports, based on sources, that the White House had ordered restrictions on the use of Starshield for Ukraine. Zelensky, who is in Brussels today to talk with European leaders about further military support, has already said that he did not believe the speed limits the army suddenly faced were caused by a malfunction. Starlink owner Elon Musk already hinted that the White House was behind it. He wrote that "restrictions on speed or use are determined by the US military and ultimately by the President of the United States."

title: Attacks on Russian data centres did not silence troll armies
lead: Last week it briefly seemed as if Russian troll armies had been brought to silence. Ukrainian drones had repeatedly struck data centres of Yandex, a large Russian technology company. President Zelensky claimed on Monday that there was "less hatred, less division and fewer provocations" to be seen on social media. A graph from cloud company Cloudflare went viral on social media. It showed a sharp drop in web traffic from Yandex bots, from which some social media users concluded that Russian troll armies were less active and less disinformation was being shared. Accounts of the MAGA movement, Reform UK supporters and the far-right German AfD were also said to have suddenly become less active. However, these claims are not supported by experts or by Cloudflare itself. On Wednesday the company published a blog post in which it analysed what lay behind the drop in web traffic. 'No evidence at all' In it, Cloudflare writes that there was "no evidence" that the attacks on the Yandex data centres had disabled social media manipulation "or otherwise disrupted malicious activity on the internet". "Cloudflare published a little graph, which was picked up everywhere", says Robert van der Noordaa, an expert on hybrid warfare and foreign interference on social media. Although the graph did show a drop in web traffic from Yandex networks, according to Van der Noordaa the wrong conclusion was drawn that troll armies had also been affected. Most people think of bots as fake accounts that spread disinformation and polarising messages on social media, but there are also other types of bots. "The bots that Cloudflare reports are not social media bots, but mainly so-called web crawlers", says Van der Noordaa. These are bots that automatically visit web pages and index them so that they can be found in search engines. Fewer pro-Kremlin posts Zelensky's team told the BBC in a response that the president had been speaking about the atmosphere on social media, which was said to have improved, and not about a decrease in bot activity. A Czech member of the European Parliament also回 returned to his post on X, in which he wrote that there was less AfD activity to be seen on social media. His post had by then been viewed more than four million times. However, the claim that there was less activity from pro-Kremlin, pro-MAGA, Reform UK and AfD accounts on social media is also refuted by other experts, such as researchers at dTeam, an American group that tracks Russian interference. dTeam tells the BBC that "no change in the traffic of known Russian accounts and bot clusters on any platform" has been observed. Bots linked to pro-Kremlin influence operations were still active on social media today. 'Platforms have responsibility' Bots cannot simply be switched off by bombardments, says Ned Mendez, head of research at Alliance4Europe, speaking to The Guardian. "As appealing as that sounds", he adds. "They are not just a few buildings that you can shut down." So what can be done against troll armies spreading fake information? Van der Noordaa says it is important to pressure social media companies to take down suspicious networks. If security services, the police or the government show that there is a coordinated network that breaks the rules, the platforms should in principle remove it, according to Van der Noordaa.

title: Limburg named 'smartest region' in the world
lead: Limburg has been named the smartest region in the world by the Intelligent Community Forum (ICF). The international think tank presented the prize to Brightlands, four campuses in the province where research is carried out into, among other things, health, AI, more sustainable chemistry and food. The ICF is a worldwide federation of 200 cities and regions that support each other in the field of innovation. Each year the think tank publishes a ranking of smart communities based on factors such as economy and social development. The ICF therefore gave the honour this year to the Brightlands campuses. The jury praises Limburg for the cooperation between government, entrepreneurs and knowledge institutions through the Brightlands campuses. There is also praise for the transition Limburg underwent after the closure of the mines, half a century ago. "After the discovery of natural gas in 1959, the region lost not only jobs, but also economic security and hope", said ICF founder Robert Bell. The Brightlands in Limburg came into being in 2014 as an initiative of the <entity id="org:provincie-limburg">provincie Limburg</entity>, educational institutions and the regional business sector, writes L1 Nieuws. The campuses in <entity id="org:gemeente-maastricht">Maastricht</entity>, <entity id="org:gemeente-sittard-geleen">Sittard-Geleen</entity>, <entity id="org:gemeente-heerlen">Heerlen</entity> and Venlo each have their own specialisation in the fields of food, chemistry, health and digitalisation. Maastricht received a campus focused on health, linked to the academic hospital. Heerlen focused on data, with the offices of pension fund ABP and the <entity id="org:zbo-centraal-bureau-voor-de-statistiek">Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek</entity>. Earlier this year it was renamed Data en AI. In Sittard-Geleen the materials campus was located on the Chemelot site. In Venlo the Brightlands campus focused on food security, making use of the infrastructure of the Floriade from 2012. <entity id="org:gemeente-eindhoven">Eindhoven</entity> Limburg had, with Brightlands, reached the last seven finalists. The other regions were Assai (Brazil), Bursa (Turkey), Hilliard (United States), Kingston (Canada), Las Rozas de Madrid (Spain) and Yunlin County (Taiwan). Last year the Canadian region of Durham was given the honour of most innovative region. In 2011 the Brainport region in Eindhoven won the title.

title: Podcast De Dag: The discovery of the clitoris
lead: For centuries the clitoris remained an underexposed organ in medical science. Although the visible 'little button' is known to many people, the complete organ turns out to be much larger and more complex than long thought. Dutch researchers from Amsterdam UMC were the first to map the complete nerve network of the clitoris in high resolution. "I saw enormously large white cables," says researcher Bernadette de Bakker. "At first I thought, what is this? They were the nerves." In this episode of De Dag, De Bakker tells how she managed to make this happen. A donated female genital organ was taken to the particle accelerator in Grenoble, France. That turned out to be quite a challenge: at first the scan was even refused, because the French researchers did not consider the clitoris an organ under their rules. Listen? You can listen to this episode of De Dag via NPO Luister and all other podcast apps. Like it? Don't forget to subscribe. The new scans show that the nerve network of the clitoris is much more extensive than scientists had thought until now. According to the researchers, this knowledge is important not only to close the knowledge gap about the female body, but can also have direct consequences for medical care. For example, during childbirth, reconstructive surgery after female genital mutilation and gender-affirming surgery, doctors can better take vulnerable nerve pathways into account. Respond? Email dedag@nos.nl. Presentation and editing: Bart Tuinman. Editorial: Judith van de Hulsbeek

title: Man must lose eye after shooting in Roosendaal, suspect arrested
lead: The <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> has arrested a man from Roosendaal suspected of shooting another man in the eye. The 44-year-old man was arrested last night by the Dienst Speciale Interventies, which is deployed against suspects who are dangerous with firearms. The victim was found on Wednesday evening in a home on Hoogstraat in Roosendaal. He had been shot in the face, presumably with a gas-powered weapon. The man also had wounds on his chest. He is expected to lose an eye and is still in hospital. According to witnesses, the two men had argued. According to the police, they quickly knew who the presumed shooter was and arrested him at home last night. He is suspected of attempted manslaughter. The weapon has not yet been found. A gas-powered weapon could be, for example, an air rifle or a CO2 pistol. Some gas-powered weapons are legal, but that does not apply to, for example, gas-powered weapons that closely resemble real firearms.

title: Rotterdam neighbourhood area ban extended to prevent unrest from returning
lead: Mayor Schouten of <entity id="org:gemeente-rotterdam">Rotterdam</entity> has extended the area ban for part of the De Esch neighbourhood by three months. "I am doing this to further reduce the attraction of the area", the mayor writes in a letter to the council. She also wants to prevent the nuisance from immediately returning after 23 October, when the area ban would initially expire. The new area ban does not apply the whole week, but from Thursday through Sunday from 23.00 to 05.00 hours. On the other days the area is kept closely monitored by the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> and boa's. "Should the situation nevertheless deteriorate, I will take additional measures where necessary", Schouten writes. The new area ban is in force until 23 January 2027. Concrete blocks Over the past years, residents of the Rotterdam neighbourhood, where just over 4000 people live, have had to deal with nuisance. Especially at night there were street races, drug use and prostitution. People who do not live in De Esch came to the neighbourhood, according to police research. The municipality had earlier already placed concrete blocks, tightened supervision and spoken with those causing nuisance. Those measures did not help enough. Eventually, in July, a unique measure was deployed: an area ban for a large part of the neighbourhood. For three months, between 23.00 and 05.00 hours, only people with a good reason were allowed to stay in the neighbourhood. Those are mainly residents and people who work there. 'Situation in De Esch considerably improved' According to the mayor, the measure has helped to reduce the nuisance. The number of nuisance reports to both police and municipality has fallen sharply. Residents and the neighbourhood council also indicate they hardly experience any nuisance at night anymore. "Over the past three months the situation has been continuously monitored, and the police further tightened supervision in the designated area", Schouten writes. "This has led to the situation in De Esch being considerably improved." When the area ban had just come into effect, people who had no business in the area still regularly came to it. In total, 140 people received an official report, 23 of them on the first evening. The municipality suspects this was because the area ban was not yet known to everyone, according to regional broadcaster Rijnmond. Different solution Mayor Schouten says she realises that an area ban is a far-reaching measure that cannot be extended indefinitely. That is why the municipality wants to work together with local residents to investigate whether a more sustainable solution can be devised. "In the recent period, thought has been given to sustainable alternative measures that could be deployed. In the period up to 23 January 2027, this process will be continued, and the neighbourhood council and residents will also be involved to consider how a sustainable solution can be reached."

title: Families and businesses near Lelystad Airport must leave due to defence expansion
lead: Four farms and six businesses must disappear, because the Ministry of Defence needs more space around Lelystad Airport. The families and businesses concerned were told this today. "I understand very well that this is a worthless message," says <entity id="person:derk-boswijk">staatssecretaris Boswijk</entity> (<entity id="org:ministerie-van-defensie">Defensie</entity>), who will also visit these people later today. Defence says it will help them through "careful contact and personal guidance". This could involve, for example, a move to another location or compensation. According to Boswijk, Defence needs the space because the F-35 fighter jets will have to fly more often. "That means you also have to train and do maintenance more," says the state secretary. "Those support units need physical space." Lelystad Airport is becoming even larger than expected due to defence goals. At first it was 150 hectares, which has now become 240 hectares. 40 hectares of that is needed to make the runway longer. The airport does not yet have a nature permit, which is needed to be able to use the airport. That application is still being prepared. "We cannot wait for that and only then do this," says Boswijk. "That would take too long." Boswijk does not expect that more homes and businesses that have to disappear due to defence expansions will follow soon. "But I cannot rule it out either, because the situation in the world is unpredictable."

title: TU Delft may not reserve study places for women
lead: <entity id="person:rianne-letschert">Minister Letschert</entity> of Education does not allow TU Delft to reserve a minimum number of places for female students for the Aerospace Engineering programme. The <entity id="org:zbo-college-voor-de-rechten-van-de-mens">College voor de Rechten van de Mens</entity> had advised that it should do so, but the ministry will not go along with this. That is a setback for the university. It wanted to introduce a quota to increase the structurally low intake of women on the programme. Last June, the College voor de Rechten van de Mens approved plans for this preferential policy, partly because according to the college it had only limited consequences for male students and served a legitimate aim. A last resort Minister Letschert says she supports the university's goal, but sees a quota as a last resort. The minister also describes introducing a quota for women at the university as time-consuming: because in current practice it is only possible to set requirements based on quality and not on sex, the Higher Education Act must be amended. Furthermore, an amendment of the law could open a debate about all sorts of other forms of preferential treatment, according to the ministry. Dominated by men The minister says she wants to achieve the university's goal in other ways within the current legislation. Among other things, by rolling out programmes to encourage women to take up jobs and courses in technology. A parliamentary motion was also adopted this month calling on <entity id="org:regering">de regering</entity> to investigate how women can be attracted to and retained in male-dominated sectors. Henri Werij, Dean of Aerospace Engineering at TU Delft, says he is disappointed by the minister's decision. "Ever since I took up the position of dean almost ten years ago, we have been working hard to get more women into the programme. Despite all the measures we have taken so far, it is only happening slowly. For real change, this quota is simply necessary."

title: Fireworks show at Erasmusbrug Rotterdam this New Year's Eve after all
lead: There will be a major fireworks show at the Erasmus Bridge in Rotterdam after all this New Year's Eve. The new Rotterdam city council had originally wanted a show with drones and lasers, but there is too little time to organise that. Moreover, it was not feasible within the set budget. Pro, D66, VVD, CDA and Volt agreed in their coalition agreement that from now on every New Year's Eve there will be a drone and laser show at the Erasmus Bridge. No more traditional and spectacular fireworks, as at the National Fireworks Show. A drone show is more environmentally friendly, the parties believe. The city council wants to set aside half a million euros per year for it. Too little time and money. Even so, a major fireworks show will be organised for the coming end-of-year celebration. Alderman Nunnely concludes after talks with experts that there is now too little time to organise an alternative show, the regional broadcaster Rijnmond reports. Moreover, a drone and laser show is not possible within the reserved budget, she writes in a letter to the municipal council. "Given the introduction of the national fireworks ban from 2026, it is desirable to offer a good alternative for consumer fireworks this year at least." To make the fireworks show possible, Rotterdam will spend roughly the same as last year, according to the alderman: that was then exactly 816,194 euros. That is therefore well over 300,000 euros more than the budget. Nunnely can cover the extra costs because the municipality is probably spending less this year than expected. From next year the executive board wants a more sustainable show. "The national fireworks show has grown into a widely attended and traditional event for many Rotterdammers and visitors," the executive board writes.

title: Billions for aging bridges and locks, at the expense of several large projects
lead: <entity id="org:kabinet">Het kabinet</entity> is allocating 18 billion euros for maintenance and renewal of aging bridges, roads, locks and other infrastructure. A large part of that amount is being taken from planned projects for which money had already been reserved. Those projects will therefore be postponed indefinitely. One of the prominent projects receiving a lot of money is the Haringvliet bridge, which connects the Hoeksche Waard with Goeree-Overflakkee. That bridge, which 66,000 people drive over every day, is in poor condition and must largely be renewed. Dry feet A considerable sum (2.3 billion euros) also goes to the pumping station in IJmuiden, which is very outdated. Renewal is important because that pumping station, according to the cabinet, keeps "dry feet" for four million people. In total, 175 roads, locks, bridges, viaducts and tunnels will be renewed or maintained. Most of them were built in the 1950s, 60s and 70s, and at many locations the steel and concrete, for example, have had their best days. These are some of the projects for which money has been set aside: "We face the biggest renewal task ever, it is time for a new reconstruction of our infrastructure", says <entity id="person:vincent-karremans">minister Karremans</entity> of Infrastructure. According to him, it is essential to ensure that the Netherlands remains protected against water and at the same time "accessible and economically strong". The selection mainly considered preservation of existing infrastructure and safety. The cabinet is also allocating money for improvements to the rail network. A number of viaducts that the high-speed line crosses between Leiden and Hoofddorp will be tackled, so that trains can run faster there: 300 kilometres per hour instead of the current 120 km/h. Furthermore, the money for the Nedersaksenlijn remains in place, more money goes to rail expansion in Meppel, and there is also a large amount for the "rollout of the European train safety system" to make the railway safer. The cabinet gives priority to renovation, but also opens its wallet for making new housing development areas accessible. Extra money is coming for four large new projects in Alkmaar, Apeldoorn, Helmond and Hengelo/Enschede. Pain But as mentioned, some projects are also being postponed to finance the above. "That of course hurts", the cabinet acknowledges in a letter to <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity>. "But this is the only way to carry out the major maintenance task." Money is being taken, among other things, from the RandstadRail between The Hague, Rotterdam and Zoetermeer and from the Rotterdam metro network. That money was meant to expand capacity. Furthermore, the widening of the lock at Kornwerderzand in Friesland will not go ahead after all. That also yields hundreds of millions. The bridges there, at the end of the Afsluitdijk, will still be replaced. The cabinet is withdrawing money from the following places, among others: In Amsterdam, part of the long-running Zuidasdok project is postponed. The project includes, among other things, the partial tunnelling of the A10 motorway at the Zuidas. For the northern section of the project there is, for now, no money. Regarding road projects, the cabinet is also taking money from the A27 between Zeewolde and Eemnes. That will not be widened for the time being. The A28 between Hoogeveen and Amersfoort, the N33 between Eemshaven and Appingedam, and the ring road around Utrecht will also not be improved for now. And Ameland is also out of luck. Because of the continually silting shipping channel to the mainland, people have been talking for ten years about a better optimal shipping connection. The minister also needs that reserved 250 million euros elsewhere. Water quality and drought control Furthermore, the cabinet is taking hundreds of millions away from improving water quality and from a programme to prevent drought. That is striking because water quality in the Netherlands is under pressure and drought is becoming an ever greater problem. For all projects that are not being carried out now, the cabinet emphasises that they are "not off the radar". Whether the House of Representatives accepts this will become clear within a few weeks. After the autumn recess the House will debate the plans. No doubt some parties have a different selection in mind than the cabinet, but whether they will get a majority for it is still the question. Moreover, says minister Karremans, the House must then also explain how it should be paid for. "If they want it differently, they must say so. But then they must also ensure they get it financed."

title: Injured in attack by settlers on olive grove on the West Bank
lead: In the village of Abu Falah in the occupied West Bank, dozens of Israeli settlers attacked Palestinians in an olive grove. Among others, a journalist who had come to cover the olive harvest was injured. The attack took place during the annual olive harvest by villagers. About eighty Israeli settlers went there, some of them with jerrycans of fuel. The settlers, masked and dressed in black, set olive trees on fire. They also threw stones at the Palestinians or fired them with a slingshot, Reuters news agency reports, based on a photographer on the spot. The Palestinians picked up the stones and threw them back. The attack was recorded by several people: Calm did not return when the Israeli army arrived. The soldiers used tear gas against the Palestinians. The Reuters photographer reports that ammunition was fired, and according to the Palestinian news agency Wafa, both Israeli soldiers and settlers fired live rounds. According to Wafa, a Palestinian was hit in his side. Also, two Palestinians were assaulted, Palestinian aid workers report. A photojournalist for The Washington Post was also injured; she is in stable condition in a hospital in Ramallah. "I was attacked and pushed to the ground", Reuters quotes the injured journalist. "Fortunately I was wearing my shrapnel vest and helmet, otherwise I probably wouldn't even be here anymore, because they kept kicking at me." The Israeli army has not yet responded to the event. West Bank The West Bank is Palestinian territory that has been illegally occupied by Israel since 1967. About 500,000 settlers live in established settlements, and at least three million Palestinians. Violence by settlers has been increasing recently. In addition to attacks in Abu Falah, according to the Palestinian news agency there were also attacks today in Burka, east of Ramallah, and in Turmus Ayya, towards the north of the West Bank. In Burka, four people were reportedly injured. In Turmus Ayya, settlers also reportedly set cars on fire. In July, Human Rights Watch reported that attacks by settlers in the area increasingly lead to forced displacement of Palestinians. The settlements of the settlers are also illegal under international law. Since 22 September, products from such settlements may no longer be imported into the Netherlands.

title: After years of discussion, financial arrangement for KNIL widows after all
lead: The widows and widowers of civil servants and military personnel who served in the Netherlands Indies government during the Second World War will nevertheless receive a financial compensation. <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> has decided this after years of political discussion. The arrangement supplements the 2015 arrangement for the KNIL soldiers and civil servants themselves. It concerns compensation for lost salary. The arrangement is only for the widows and widowers, not for their heirs. Those concerned must submit an application themselves. This can be done from 1 February 2027. After the application, individual archival research will be conducted to see whether the applicant qualifies for the arrangement. There are no files or archives in which this information is centrally stored. "I fully realize that full restitution can never be offered to these widows and widowers", says <entity id="person:mirjam-sterk">minister Sterk</entity> of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-volksgezondheid-welzijn-en-sport">VWS</entity>. "What happened to them during and after the Second World War can never be reversed or undone." Japanese occupation Civil servants, teachers and military personnel in the Dutch East Indies received no salary during the Japanese occupation. The discussion about this began directly after the war. But the Dutch government was not legally obliged to pay the back salaries and held out. It took until 2015 before KNIL soldiers received compensation of 25,000 euros from the government for their back salary. At that time, the then cabinet reached an agreement with Indisch Platform 2.0, which supported Indian and Moluccan soldiers. Around 600 people registered for this arrangement.

title: Neanderthal Shanidar A was cared for and murdered 75,000 years ago
lead: Scientists have stumbled upon one of the oldest murder cases in the history of hominins. Research indicates that the Neanderthal Shanidar A was probably killed with a spear in the Stone Age. At the same time, the researchers have found indications that the victim first received care from others for years. The male Neanderthal was buried around 75,000 years ago in the Shanidar cave in northern Iraq. Seven years ago the skeleton was excavated and since then it has been scrutinized by scientists. According to the researchers, this has yielded "significant new perspectives" on life and death among Neanderthals. The results have been published on the website of the renowned scientific platform Scientific Reports . It describes how the deep wound in the shoulder blade of Shanidar A was almost certainly caused by a wooden spear. Deliberate attack. It could have been an accident while hunting. According to researcher and bio-anthropologist Emma Pomeroy, however, that scenario is not obvious. So much force must have been used to pierce the body completely that the situation "has characteristics of a deliberate attack to kill someone," she tells the American news network CNN . The angle of the wound also suggests that attacker and victim stood directly facing each other. But who the perpetrator was and what the motive was will logically not come to light after tens of millennia. Pomeroy has also examined other Neanderthal bodies in the Shanidar cave. In the photo below from 2024 you can see the researcher, with on the right the skull of woman Shanidar Z and on the left a reconstruction of what this Neanderthal looked like: It rarely happens that traces of murder are found on Stone Age fossils. Since Homo sapiens switched from hunting and gathering to agriculture, that has become a different story. Since then, people have lived together in larger groups and countless skeletons have been found with signs of deliberate violence. So murder also occurred among Neanderthals, the researchers point to the fate of Shanidar A. The other side of the story is that he also appears to have received help from other Neanderthals for a long time. Cooking food The forty-year-old had namely suffered a severe injury to his teeth, years before he was violently killed. To survive this he must have had help from relatives, who for example cooked and mashed food, says Pomeroy. According to the archaeologist, it is all together a human story of Shanidar A. "On the one hand there is evidence of a terribly violent end. On the other hand, this was clearly an individual who was cared for during his life."

title: Podcast De Stemming: Dolphins, a pincushion and an asylum operetta
lead: Minister Van den Brink of Asylum went again to <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">de Eerste Kamer</entity> to defend his asylum plans. This time it went a bit better than a few months ago. But Van den Brink immediately got another problem, because JA21 suddenly sets tough demands on asylum. Meanwhile, VVD leader Yesilgöz is not entirely comfortable with her own base, and the US once again came under fire over the International Criminal Court. De Stemming This episode of De Stemming by Vullings and De Rooy can be listened to at <entity id="org:zbo-nederlandse-publieke-omroep">NPO</entity> Luister. You can also find all previous episodes there. Just like on all other well-known podcast channels. About this podcast Political journalists Joost Vullings (EenVandaag, AVROTROS) and Marleen de Rooy (NOS) go through the Hague week every Friday, with sharp analyses, rumours and predictions. Want to respond? Email destemming@nos.nl.

title: US sanctions against the ICC already putting ABN Amro in a tight spot
lead: For six months, the Netherlands and the European Union tried to persuade the United States through diplomacy to call off the planned sanctions against the International Criminal Court (ICC). But although the sanctions are only due to take effect in April, time is already running short in practice. Companies that provide services to the ICC fear the long arm of US justice if they still do business with the court in half a year. ABN Amro is in a difficult position because of the situation, RTL Z already reported yesterday. The ICC has a bank account at ABN Amro to receive donations, for example, as stated on the website of the court, which is based in The Hague. When asked, ABN Amro says it never comments on individual clients. But the bank adds that it always abides by applicable laws and regulations. Major consequences If the bank, still 20 percent state-owned, listens to <entity id="person:rob-jetten">premier Jetten</entity> and does not drop the ICC as a client, the consequences could be enormous. In the US, ABN Amro still holds a US banking license, for a division that processes transactions on the financial markets for large traders. This so-called clearing bank accounted for 20 percent of ABN Amro's annual profit last year. Through that US banking license, ABN Amro is in the grip of US justice. ING experienced this, for example, when the division in Caribbean Netherlands transferred money to Cuba and Iran. That led to a huge US fine for the Dutch bank. Earlier incidents at Dutch banks due to US sanctions: Prime Minister Jetten had initially used firm language at the United Nations General Assembly in New York to make clear that the US must keep its hands off the ICC. After the sanctions were nevertheless announced shortly afterwards, he hoped that in the meantime "a suitable solution" for the ICC could be found with the US. Patience Yesterday the American ambassador in the Netherlands made clear that there is little to talk about. "Our patience with the court was met with escalation instead of reform, and dawdling instead of decisiveness. President Donald Trump has said: 'Not anymore", wrote Ambassador Joe Popolo in a letter to the editor in the FD. Popolo states that the sanctions against the ICC will only be lifted if "every threat to American citizens is neutralized". In other words: if the court officially records that it will not pursue Americans. The officials in The Hague are meanwhile keeping quiet about the ICC. Behind the scenes, it is clear that they are mainly looking for a way for the court to keep functioning if the US sanctions are nevertheless imposed. How the ICC should work without cloud services, email and bank accounts is for now a black diplomatic gap. The US has been targeting the ICC for years:

title: President of Croatia is ashamed of Nazi remarks by Hajduk Split fans
lead: Croatian President Milanovic condemns the chants that supporters of football club Hajduk Split sang yesterday before the match against Ajax. He calls the chants "unacceptable and shameful". Members of the hardcore fans of Hajduk Split sang lyrics on the way to the stadium such as "stand up, Adolf Hitler" and "Auschwitz, Auschwitz". They also sang about "crushing Jews". At the march to the stadium in Split, a small Volkswagen drove at the front with a coffin on its roof bearing the text Ajax. The Amsterdam club had called on supporters traveling to the Conference League match to not wear visible Ajax clothing and to avoid the city centre. Things also went wrong during the match. In the 75th minute the supporters group Torcida set off a large quantity of flares. This caused a lot of smoke and the referee halted the match for twelve minutes. The players were sent inside. The board of the Croatian club immediately after the match offered apologies to Ajax and to the European football association UEFA. The club says it does not wish to be associated with this kind of expression. Hajduk Split can expect a high fine and must also take into account matches without spectators or with empty sections. Setting off fireworks and flares is a serious violation of UEFA rules. The club already received a fine of 56,000 euros in August for incidents during a qualifying match against Polish club Raków. Hajduk Split also received a conditional sentence: if the club again goes wrong, at least a thousand seats in the stadium must remain closed for two years. It is now waiting to see what penalty UEFA imposes. According to Croatian media, it is also being investigated whether UEFA can act over the incidents before the match. In the days before the match the city was already restless. In the night of Wednesday to Thursday the police already arrested 57 people after supporters of Ajax and Hajduk Split had sought confrontation with each other.

title: Community service for rapper Appa after 'doxing' of Jewish woman and journalist
lead: Rapper Appa has been found guilty of intimidating a Jewish woman and a journalist from NOS. He did so by 'doxing' them, in other words by publicly sharing their personal information. The 43-year-old rapper receives forty hours of community service, half of which is suspended with a probation period of two years. Earlier, the <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> had requested sixty hours of community service. The judge arrived at a lighter sentence because he had never before been prosecuted for such an action. The police judge in Utrecht speaks of serious offences, from which the two victims suffered greatly. "Both were approached in unpleasant ways by people who were stirred up by the posts." The rapper was acquitted of a third case. According to the judge, rapper Appa, with his posts on social media, infringed on the privacy of the victims and caused feelings of insecurity. Actions of this kind can lead followers or others to break the law and commit acts. The judge holds this against him, according to the ruling. What is doxing? Doxing is the public sharing of sensitive personal data in order to intimidate. Since 1 January 2024 this has been prohibited and punishable by law. According to the government, publicly disclosing personal data is very common and often has serious consequences for the victims. Doxing is often aimed at journalists, politicians, judges or care workers. In March 2024, the personal details of relatives of Israeli soldiers in the Netherlands were spread online. They subsequently faced hatred and threats. One of the instigators was rapper and activist Appa, who on his Instagram account shared photos and personal details of at least one Israeli-Dutch woman subject to conscription in Israel and of this woman's mother. In doing so, he posted hateful texts and the call 'fight!'. NOS journalist A NOS journalist who wrote two articles on this matter then also became a victim of doxing by the rapper. He posted a photo of her with text including "and that is why you, just like that terrorist, will be exposed. (..) see what you do." The police judge rejected the defendant's defence in both cases. He argued that he only wanted to gather information about the Jewish woman for a possible lawsuit against her. In the case of the NOS journalist, he wanted to correct reporting that he considered incorrect. Fear and nuisance But the judge concludes that the 43-year-old artist must have realised that his conduct would lead to fear and nuisance for the victims. In the case of the journalist, he moreover points out how doxing "seriously hinders" the practice of the profession and her fear is fuelled. "We are very satisfied with the ruling," responds Wilma Haan, deputy editor-in-chief of NOS Nieuws. "We are glad that the judge, in addition to the personal burden the victims, including our colleague, have suffered from this, has also paid attention to the chilling effect on journalism. It must never become normal for journalists to be personally intimidated because of their work." It is not yet known whether the convicted man will appeal; he has two weeks to decide.

title: Pope on the mend, celebrates mass in hospital
lead: Pope Leo XIV is getting better and better. According to the Vatican, this is apparent from new blood tests and X-rays at the Gemelli hospital, where a malignant nodule on his lung was removed this week. This afternoon he celebrated mass in the hospital. He also distributed communion. Hospital staff and members of the Vatican police attended the mass. The pope thanked the care workers for the care they provide "for vulnerable patients, and especially for what they have done and continue to do for him", the Vatican writes. Phone call with Putin The pope continues with breathing exercises and, according to the Vatican, can now also carry out his daily activities independently again. Today, for example, he called Russian President Putin from the hospital. In the phone call the pope expressed his concern for the humanitarian situation around the Ukrainian city of Olesjky. He called for a ceasefire so that humanitarian aid such as food and medication can be delivered. Olesjky lies at the front in Ukraine and has been occupied by Russia for years. It is one of a number of Ukrainian cities that have been completely cut off from the outside world. They are surrounded by Russian landmines, and the area is also under constant surveillance by Russian drones. There are growing international concerns about the situation in Olesjky; famine threatens. Putin reportedly responded positively to the pope's words. "It has been agreed to work together on this", the Kremlin says. Sunday prayer goes ahead On Tuesday the pope was admitted to the Gemelli hospital and that same day he underwent surgery. During that operation it became clear that he has a common form of lung cancer. During the procedure the lower part of his right lung was removed. The pope is expected to remain in hospital for a number of days. According to the Vatican, the weekly midday prayer on Sunday, which is normally led by the pope, will go ahead as usual.

title: Fewer trains around Utrecht due to farewell drinks for train traffic controllers
lead: Since 14.30 hours, fewer trains have been running around Utrecht due to a shortage of train traffic controllers. The shortage is partly due to a farewell drinks event for "two highly valued colleagues" at ProRail. That is what a spokesperson for the rail infrastructure manager told NOS after reports by RTL Nieuws. Because of the farewell drinks, ProRail did not manage to get enough staff on duty. As a result, until about halfway through the evening, fewer trains run on the routes Amersfoort - Den Haag, Rotterdam - Utrecht and Bodegraven - Utrecht. The autumn holiday also contributes to the failure to make the work roster work: many colleagues are on holiday and there is a lot of sickness. ProRail says it has "done everything" this week to get the planning sorted. The spokesperson says it finds this "incredibly annoying" for passengers. The spokesperson does not know whether an attempt was made to postpone the drinks. ProRail has been struggling with a shortage of train traffic controllers for some time. The company has difficulty finding new staff and moreover cannot easily train traffic controllers itself, according to the latest annual report. Train traffic controllers monitor train traffic 24 hours a day and intervene in the event of an emergency. Without them, no trains can run.

title: Problems at Albert Heijn not yet resolved, no delivery until Tuesday
lead: The IT problems at Albert Heijn continue. Until and including Tuesday, groceries cannot be delivered, the supermarket chain reports. Scheduled deliveries have been cancelled. Yesterday AH still said it would not be able to deliver to homes at least until Sunday, due to the hacking attack of last weekend. It remains impossible for the time being to place new orders. "We are doing everything we can to deliver groceries to customers at home again from the second half of the week", the supermarket chain said. The stores are being restocked several times a day again, Albert Heijn says. The prices on the shelves are correct again, but the personal discounts and loyalty point campaigns are still not available. The customer service line is also still not reachable and the app is not yet fully working. Hacking attack On Sunday, Albert Heijn took its systems offline due to a so-called "cybersecurity incident". According to sources of the NOS, it was a hacking attack. Who is behind it is still unclear. According to the chain, there are so far no indications that personal data has been stolen.

title: Dutch cloud sector demands clarity over server seizure at US request
lead: The Dutch trade association for the cloud and internet sector, Dutch Cloud Community (DCC), has serious concerns about a server that the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> seized this week in Amsterdam-Oost. That seizure was at the request of American authorities. It concerns a server of the Italian anti-capitalist and anti-fascist internet service provider Autistici/Inventati (A/I), which was located at the Amsterdam Science Park. According to DCC, the course of events seems to create a blank cheque for the US to request data, without it being clear whether an independent Dutch legal review preceded it. The trade association says it has sent a brandbrief to the police to get clarity on the legal basis for the seizure and the course of events. "Without a clear Dutch review, the Netherlands is losing the trust of the organisations and companies that store their data here", the organisation says. DCC recognises that international assistance is important in combating crime, but warns that it must not be misused to suppress political expression. OM: data not yet shared. The <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> in Amsterdam says in a written response to news agency ANP that the seizure was carried out on the basis of the treaty between the Netherlands and the US on mutual legal assistance in criminal matters. In this case there would have been no ground for refusal for the OM. The OM further states that the seized data have not yet been shared with the US. Anti-capitalist internet service provider A/I is a left-wing Italian internet provider that until recently, for about 25 years and for activist reasons, offered free email services and web hosting to around 20,000 organisations and activists worldwide who stand up for civil rights and equality. According to the US, the Italian provider is a terrorist organisation that provides services to "extreme left-wing organisations". Those organisations are said to include "Antifa cells", among others. Antifa is the international decentralised protest movement that combats fascism, without a clear structure or central leadership. A/I dissolved itself. After the US imposed sanctions at the end of August, A/I decided a good week later to dissolve as a precaution. The organisation said it wanted to prevent others from being put in danger, as stated in an online statement. Because of the US sanctions, A/I lost access to its domain name, among other things, its PayPal account was withdrawn and its regular bank account was blocked. In the days before the blockade, an unsolicited wave of donations came in from people who wanted to support A/I, NRC reported earlier. The Italian bank Banca Etica, where A/I had an account, decided to block it after the sanctions, out of fear that possible US secondary sanctions could also endanger services to 130,000 other customers and members. The bank did, however, condemn the conduct of the US government.

title: Zelensky asks Europe for 70 billion in extra support as relations with the US cool
lead: "We need financial support, air defence and help getting through the winter." That is what Ukrainian President Zelensky said ahead of the second day of the EU summit in Brussels. In a speech afterwards he was more specific: Ukraine is asking its European allies for an extra 70 billion euros, "for defence, for weapons and for our resilience". Zelensky's appeal comes at a time when Ukraine is under heavy pressure. His country is on the eve of a harsh winter, and there are fears that Russia will try to hit the Ukrainian energy sector even harder. The capital Kyiv in particular is attacked daily with ballistic missiles, and the supply of Patriot missiles needed to intercept those projectiles is almost exhausted. During a press conference at the summit in Brussels, Zelensky was asked about President Trump, who has criticised him several times in recent days: Allies who want to support Ukraine in this can only do so to a limited extent. European countries depend largely on the Patriot systems from the US for air defence, but that country, partly because of the war in Iran, has a shortage itself and is keeping its stock for itself. Even so, Zelensky states that European allies still have enough air defence missiles to help Ukraine get through the winter. Defence expert Patrick Bolder of the Haags Centrum voor Strategische Studies suspects that Zelensky wants the Patriot missiles from Greece and Spain. The shelf life of their Patriot missiles is nearly expired. Thinking more economically: A European alternative to the Patriot air defence system does not exist yet. Ukraine tested a new air defence missile this summer, but according to Ukraine the first FP-7.x missiles of the so-called Freyja system can only be deployed early next year. "Where Ukraine still shot down cheap drones with expensive missiles in 2025, they now think more economically," says Bolder. For this reason Zelensky went to the Gulf region this year, to prevent Patriot missiles from being used against cheaper drones. Which weapon is used at which moment is a constant competition, the defence expert says. "When the Ukrainians had an answer to the Russian drones, Russia began firing drones with jet engines, which Ukraine found hard to intercept," he says. "Now that Ukraine is better able to deal with those, Russia is firing ballistic missiles again, because Ukraine cannot stop them." Still, about 300 Spanish and Greek air defence missiles are not the solution. If Russia launches dozens of ballistic missiles, as it did on Wednesday, and Ukraine uses two air defence missiles per missile, that stock will quickly run out, says the HCSS expert. In April the Netherlands bought an extra American Patriot system, despite the wish to become less dependent on the US. It will not be delivered until in a few years. According to Bolder, the fact that there is no alternative yet is because European countries have always trusted the US since the Cold War, and never thought the consumption of Patriot missiles would become so high. That was "strategically blind and naive", Bolder thinks. The turning point came after the Russian invasion, when countries agreed in 2025 on the raised NATO norm. "Now the realisation is coming that this dependence is not good." But, the defence expert adds: "it certainly takes fifteen years before you have a fully fledged defence industry up and running." Meanwhile, US President Trump has regularly lashed out at Zelensky in recent weeks. According to Trump, it is time for a new Ukrainian leader, "who can make a deal". Trump hopes that by putting pressure on Zelensky, Ukraine will stop attacking the Russian oil sector. That matters to the US president because last week he closed a deal with the Kremlin on the import of Russian diesel. Besides the Russian attacks and the difficult relationship with Trump, Ukraine is also struggling with obtaining intelligence. The Americans have a large satellite that can detect missile launches early from space. That went wrong this week, when Ukraine was not informed about a Russian air attack. According to the US this was due to a technical defect, but according to Bolder it shows how dependent we are on American technology. Starlink, which Ukraine uses to control drones, also proved unreliable this week. Still, the Ukrainians still need it. According to Zelensky there is no fully fledged alternative to the services of the company of tech billionaire Elon Musk. However, he said today that Ukraine is cooperating with countries such as France to obtain more capacity in this area.

title: American media: new White House spokesperson gone again within a week
lead: Five days after taking office, the new White House spokesperson Katie Zacharia is going to leave again. That is what various American media, including CNN , The New York Times and Fox News , write, based on sources within the White House. President Trump told journalists today that he has asked Zacharia to "reconsider" her role as his main spokesperson. It is unclear whether Trump has fired her. Fox News reported after Trump's statement that the 41-year-old Zacharia is on her way out and speaks of a "gradual departure". The New York Times writes, based on three sources, that Trump has fired her. With that, Zacharia goes down in the books as the shortest-serving press spokesperson of the White House. Rocky debut Zacharia was appointed last Friday as successor to Karoline Leavitt. Her first (and only) press conference as White House spokesperson went particularly badly this week. Zacharia did not seem to be well versed in the subject matter and, among other things, misspoke. For example, she spoke of "my president" when she meant her husband. The briefing lasted less than a quarter of an hour and she only let Trump-friendly journalists speak. They were allowed to ask three questions. This week she came under fire because of her past. Over two years, Zacharia shared more than ten posts on social media in which she presented herself as a lawyer, while there is no evidence that she passed her bar exam. Today, in an interview with Fox News, she indeed said she is not a lawyer. Zacharia is considered a Trump supporter and called him, among other things, " the greatest president in American history ". She previously worked, among other things, as a communications adviser at Trump Media & Technology Group, which manages Trump's Truth Social network, and as deputy press secretary for the US Department of Homeland Security. Successor to Leavitt Her predecessor, the 28-year-old Leavitt, stepped down as White House spokesperson in August because she wanted to spend more time with her family and two young children. She was the youngest ever to hold that office. Like Zacharia, Leavitt is an avid MAGA supporter and was considered one of Trump's confidants. She had a communication style similar to the American president's. She regularly confronted journalists head-on. Her departure was a big loss for Trump.

title: After devastating flood, child trafficking now threatens in Nepal
lead: On the upper floors of a bleak building, some of whose outer walls are missing, an employee of a Nepalese aid organisation serves hot food. Although the building is still under construction, it is good enough for now to serve as a canteen. Nearly two months after a flood wiped out entire villages in Nepal, hard work is being done on reconstruction. In Uttargaya, a small town in the disaster area, around 45 children are being cared for whose parents are missing. Opposite the improvised canteen is another building with dormitory rooms. "It is a sad situation, many of the children do not even know that their parents have died. They think they are still missing and could return at any moment," says aid worker Raunak Raj Sarraf. Temporary reception locations Houses are being dug out and, where possible, emergency bridges are being built to restore transport from village to village. Meanwhile, Nepalese people are waiting in tent camps and temporary reception locations until they can return home. It is precisely there that children who have lost parents or been separated from family are especially vulnerable. For them the danger has not yet passed. The tents with large logos of aid organisations on them are, according to Sarraf, a kind of target for human traffickers. With people, emergency packages and aid workers coming and going, there is not always a clear view of children who are alone there. Sheer despair Children whose parents survived the disaster but lost everything are also at risk, says local aid worker Rasmita Tamang. "They no longer have money to support their children or send them to school." They are therefore willing to hand their children over to unreliable parties. Out of sheer despair. Aid organisations in Nepal warn that trafficking networks become more active during disasters. This also proved true during the previous major disaster, the 2015 earthquake. With promises of good schooling or work, children are taken to the capital Kathmandu, out of sight of aid workers. "Nepal has an open border with India, where they are taken via Kathmandu to be further trafficked," according to Sarraf. The children are used there as household help. Sometimes they end up in circuses where they have to perform for money. Young girls risk ending up in forced prostitution through brothels. Rasmita Tamang sees that children are also being smuggled to China, because many Nepalese travel there to do business: "Children end up in special Nepalese bars to work, or they end up in prostitution." Figures on the number of children who fall into the hands of these networks are not available. During the 2015 earthquake, local aid organisations estimated that hundreds of children may have been trafficked in this way. "It is good that the government has allowed fewer outside aid organisations in this time, so there is less confusion about who is doing what," says Sarraf. According to him, there is therefore more oversight. Role of government Even so, he wants the government to do more to get the children out of the tents and place them in reception locations such as the one in Uttargaya. Although the building leaves much to be desired, there is much better visibility of the children here. The aid organisation ensures they keep going to school, despite the difficult situation they are in. In one of the dormitories Priya is drawing. Because of the disaster she has been separated from her parents. She cannot reach the village where they are because of the poor roads. She draws the riverbank and the houses that stood there before: "I am trying to remember it, but it is not going well," she explains. According to aid worker Tamang, there is one difference with the past during this disaster: "The government listens much better to the experts of local organisations who advise on combating child trafficking". This gives hope that fewer children will fall into the hands of traffickers this time.

title: Chaos at UN climate panel complete: no agreement, no budget and no report?
lead: The fierce political battle over the most influential climate report in the world appears to have been settled in favour of the oil and coal countries. After a week of discussion, no agreement has been reached on the timing of when that report should be published. The question now is whether it can still appear in time for an important climate summit in 2028. The chaos at the authoritative UN climate panel IPCC is thereby complete. The discussion about the publication timeline has never derailed so completely. That IPCC chair Jim Skea has now ended the meeting without an agreement on that timeline or the budgets is seen as a victory for a number of countries with fossil fuel interests, who want to delay the report until after the 2028 climate summit. In particular, the oil and coal countries Saudi Arabia and India want at all costs to prevent this bundling of available knowledge about global warming from arriving in time for that summit. That has to do with the fact that precisely at that moment it must be assessed how much progress has been made to achieve the climate goals of Paris. There it was agreed to limit global warming to 2 degrees, and preferably to 1.5 degrees. Assessing international climate policy becomes much more difficult if the latest knowledge is not available. Torpedoed Before closing the meeting, IPCC chair Skea still tried to get the budget for 2027 approved, so that the hundreds of international scientists can continue working on their part of the report. However, this was blocked by the Indians and Saudis. Together with a number of poorer countries, they argue for delaying the IPCC report, according to them in order to give climate scientists in poorer countries more time to do their work. That way, those poorer countries, with fewer climate scientists and less money, would be better represented in the final IPCC reports. Critics warn that countries such as Saudi Arabia, India, Russia and China are mainly using that legitimate discussion to protect their fossil fuel interests. Whether the chance that the report arrives on time has now definitively been torpedoed has not yet been said out loud, but it has become much more difficult. In any case, in the first months of 2027 it becomes practically impossible to continue the work normally, which makes for a very short timeframe for the climate scientists involved with their already tight deadlines. World leaders That the 195 countries present this week in Ethiopia did not agree is very damaging to the Nobel Prize-winning IPCC. The panel, with its bundling of all climate knowledge, is regarded as a relatively stable party in an otherwise thoroughly politicised climate debate. Earlier this year, President Trump withdrew the United States from the IPCC, causing the panel to lose an important funder. Although the US has by no means always played the most enthusiastic leading role in climate diplomacy, American climate scientists and their work are seen as almost indispensable. The US also had a moderating effect politically on countries such as Saudi Arabia. Experts do not rule out that the current impasse has partly arisen because of the US departure. The meeting has now ended and the delegations of the countries present and independent climate scientists are left confused about how to proceed. A start to an answer to that question may come sooner than expected. At the end of next month, numerous world leaders travel to the international climate summit COP31 in Turkey. Behind the scenes, it is said that the struggle over the IPCC will continue there.

title: Missing 29-year-old woman found dead in Amsterdam, police assume a crime
lead: A 29-year-old woman was found dead in the water on the Amsteldijk in Amsterdam this morning. She died as a result of a crime, the police said. The woman had been missing since 4 October. Her family reported her missing to the police on 5 October. At 8.30 a.m. this morning the police were alerted to a suspicious situation on the Amsteldijk in the Amsterdam-Zuid district. This evening it was announced that the woman was found there. The police say they cannot yet provide information on exactly what happened to her. RAI The 29-year-old Hajar was last seen on 4 October near the RAI congress centre in Amsterdam-Zuid. She was then cycling together with an unknown man in the direction of the Buitenveldert neighbourhood, the police reported earlier this week. At that time the police and her family already said they were seriously worried about her well-being.

title: Thousands of insulin pens stolen from Novo Nordisk from a Dutch wholesaler
lead: Thousands of Novo Nordisk insulin pens were stolen from a Dutch wholesaler last week, the Danish medicine producer reports. The stolen pens could possibly be resold via illegal channels. Novo Nordisk warns of serious health risks if the pens are used incorrectly. According to the company, there is a chance the pens will be offered as weight-loss medication. The stolen pens do, however, contain insulin and not the active substance of weight-loss drugs, semaglutide. The company also produces the injectable weight-loss drug Wegovy. 'Do not buy it via illegal channels' Using insulin in people who do not have diabetes can lead to a blood sugar level that is too low. It can cause symptoms such as trembling, sweating and nausea. People may also become confused or even lose consciousness. This year someone was in a coma for several hours after using a so-called weight-loss pen that turned out to contain insulin. In the worst case, use can even lead to death. Novo Nordisk urges people to only use medicines if they have received a prescription for them from their doctor. "Medicines must under no circumstances be bought or traded via illegal channels, including social media, online marketplaces, gyms or informal networks." The <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> is investigating the theft. According to Novo Nordisk, measures have been taken to prevent this from happening again.

title: Frustration and disappointment after announcement of cabinet infrastructure plans
lead: Frustration and disappointment can be heard from various corners of the country following the announcement of the cabinet's plans for maintenance and renewal of aging bridges, roads, locks and other infrastructure. Today <entity id="person:vincent-karremans">minister Karremans</entity> and <entity id="person:annet-bertram">staatssecretaris Bertram</entity> announced that a total of 18 billion euros will be set aside for this. A large part of that amount is being taken from planned projects, which will be postponed as a result. Among others, the widening of the Kornwerderzand lock complex in <entity id="org:provincie-fryslan">Friesland</entity> will not go ahead, and the accessibility of <entity id="org:gemeente-ameland">Ameland</entity> will also not be tackled for now. "Extremely disappointing," says acting mayor <entity id="person:tytsy-willemsma">Tytsy Willemsma</entity> of Ameland. She says it has been shown for "more than ten years" that this ferry connection is not sustainable. In 2008 the national government itself had urged the widening of the lock at Kornwerderzand, but that too will not go ahead for now. Sijbrand de Vries, director of De Vries Scheepsbouw, builds superyachts and has been waiting for years for a wider lock. He calls it "a hard blow." "This file has been on the table for so long." These are some of the projects for which money has (and has not) been allocated: Elsewhere in the country there is disappointment too. In Brabant, for example, improving the N65 between Den Bosch and <entity id="org:gemeente-tilburg">Tilburg</entity> has been pushed back indefinitely. "It is already the sixth time in barely three years," says deputy Stijn Smeulders to news agency ANP. 81 million euros had been reserved for the N65, "an important traffic artery in the heart of our province." The provinces <entity id="org:provincie-zeeland">Zeeland</entity> and <entity id="org:provincie-zuid-holland">Zuid-Holland</entity> and the Metropolitan Region <entity id="org:gemeente-rotterdam">Rotterdam</entity> <entity id="org:gemeente-s-gravenhage">Den Haag</entity> say they "had hoped for more vision for the future" from the cabinet in the choices that have been made. The provinces had hoped for more investment in widening motorways and public transport. "The cabinet assesses projects solely within the limited financial resources made available," reads a joint statement. The replacement of the HRMK railway bridge at <entity id="org:gemeente-leeuwarden">Leeuwarden</entity> will also not go ahead for now. Deputy Matthijs de Vries (ChristenUnie) tells news agency ANP that for Friesland this is "very painful." In <entity id="org:gemeente-amsterdam">Amsterdam</entity> part of the long-running Zuidasdok project is being postponed. The project includes, among other things, the partial tunnelling of the A10 motorway at the Zuidas. For the northern section of the project there is, for the time being, no money. 175 projects renewed or maintained In total, the plans cover the renewal or maintenance of 175 roads, locks, bridges, viaducts and tunnels. Most of them were built in the 1950s, 1960s and 1970s, and in many places the steel and concrete, for example, have reached the end of their life. The cabinet is also allocating money for improvements to the rail network. For all projects that are not being carried out now, the cabinet stresses that they are "not off the radar." After the autumn recess <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> will debate the plans.

title: Belgian Dave De K. guilty of manslaughter and abduction of toddler Dean
lead: In Ghent, Belgium, Dave De K. has been found guilty of the manslaughter and abduction of the 4-year-old Dean. His ex-girlfriend Romy W. has been acquitted of the abduction. Four years ago, the body of the toddler was found at the work island Neeltje Jans in Zeeland. This month, gruesome details came out about what happened before his death. De K. said that he had had a fit of rage in the car and had then hit Dean several times with his fist. He said he was not angry at Dean, but frustrated with his own relationship and life. Dean's mother was voluntarily admitted to the psychiatric ward of the hospital in Sint-Niklaas, near Antwerp, at the time of the incident. De K. and Romy W. were to care for the toddler during her stay. Driving around all day with the body After the mistreatment the boy lived for a few more hours. De K. dressed Dean in his apartment. He then got into the car with the child and drove to his drug dealer in Koudekerke. According to De K., the toddler was largely conscious but kept fading away. During a car ride Dean reportedly said he needed to pee. De K. helped the 4-year-old out of the car onto a hard shoulder. There the child collapsed and died. De K. drove around Zeeland for another day with Dean on the back seat. He had laid a blanket over him. Eventually he left the body behind at Neeltje Jans. Possibly 30 years in prison De K. has now been convicted by an assize jury for Dean's death. He has also been found guilty of possessing images of child sexual abuse. The man could receive a prison sentence of 30 years. It is not the first time he has gone to prison. In 2010 De K. received a ten-year prison sentence for the fatal abuse of his 2-year-old stepson. His lawyers have told Belgian media that De K. is aware there is no place for him in society. "He has indicated that he may find his place is better in prison." Romy W. is not guilty of abducting Dean, as according to the people's jury there was too little evidence for that. However, she is guilty of possessing and distributing images of child sexual abuse. By her own account, she forwarded the images from De K. to herself in order to confront him with them. The sentences for De K. and W. will be determined on Monday.

title: Chinese man evades police for 24 years by taking over the identity of his dead twin brother
lead: A Chinese man who was involved in a robbery in 2002 has been arrested 24 years later. That is what Chinese media report. He managed to stay out of the hands of the police for years by assuming the identity of his deceased twin brother. In 2002, seven men carried out a robbery in Yuhuan, in the province of Zhejiang in eastern China. They abducted a man and robbed him of his money and valuables. The police quickly arrested six suspects, but the seventh man, with the surname Chen, escaped. The police searched extensively for Chen, but did not find him. Five years later, in 2007, the police in Yuhuan received a report from the province of Anhui. The man was said to have died in a traffic accident. The police decided to close the case. Police check Nineteen years later, during a routine check, the police in Yuhuan discovered something striking: a tip from the province of Anhui. There were indications that a man had been using the identity of his deceased twin brother for years. Detectives became suspicious and reopened the file on the 2002 robbery. They compared the identities, places of birth and family ties of those involved, and this led to the setting up of a special investigation team. The team travelled to Anhui and soon found out that Chen was still alive. He appeared to be leading a quiet life and thought he could keep up his deception forever. In the 2007 accident, Chen's slightly older twin brother, who had the same surname, had died. The younger brother, the suspect in the robbery, had the official documents of the deceased brother altered. He submitted a new photo for the identity card, nine days after his twin brother's death. Archived photos During the investigation in Anhui, relatives of the brothers still defended the fugitive Chen by keeping up his lie. But by studying archived, old identity photos, the officers managed to gain clarity. Eventually the officers came to the ex-girlfriend of the deceased brother, who confirmed the identity swap. The fugitive Chen was arrested in June, but Chinese media are only now reporting the news. The Chinese man faces a prison sentence of three to ten years.

title: Fire in Arnhem flat that had previously been cleared due to squatters
lead: A fire broke out on Friday evening in a flat in Arnhem. The flat had been cleared and boarded up earlier in the day. Squatters were living there. As far as is known, nobody was injured. The fire broke out around 22:30 and was extinguished about an hour later. According to De Gelderlander, someone was still in the sealed building on the Paasberglaan during the fire. He did not suffer serious injuries. He has been fined because he was not allowed to enter the building, the newspaper reports. It is not known what caused the fire.

title: Rapper Diddy transferred to another prison, 'lived like a VIP in cell'
lead: The convicted American rapper Diddy has been transferred to another prison. According to American media, he is said to be living a life of luxury in prison. He was also involved in a fight this week. Sean 'Diddy' Combs was in a cell in New Jersey, but is now moving to Allenwood, in the state of Pennsylvania. NBC News had already painted a shocking picture of Diddy's former prison. Fellow inmates reportedly did all kinds of things for him, such as cooking, cleaning, making his bed and giving him massages. In addition, Diddy reportedly had cognac smuggled in and had access to a mobile phone, with which he could use social media and look at nude photos of an ex-girlfriend. According to NBC, he lived the life of a VIP in prison. Fight This week, according to entertainment site TMZ, Diddy was involved in a fight. He reportedly fought with a fellow inmate. The reason for the fight is not known. Diddy then had to be treated for his injuries outside the prison. The American prison system does not say why Diddy was transferred. However, because of the uproar, he reportedly had 41 days of sentence reduction for good behaviour taken away. As a result, he will now not be released until 2 March 2028. Sex case Diddy was sentenced a year ago to four years and two months in prison in a sex case. He was found guilty of sex trafficking for the purpose of prostitution. During the trial, women described being beaten, threatened, sexually abused and blackmailed by him. One of his ex-girlfriends spoke of drug marathons in which she had to perform sexual acts with male sex workers. Diddy filmed this and gave instructions. The rapper has never admitted guilt.

title: British nurse swindled care home resident out of 9 ton
lead: A nurse from Wales has been suspended because she stole money for years from a very elderly woman in a care home. It involved many tons, with which she paid for cosmetic procedures, among other things, and had her house renovated. According to the BBC, Rebecca Louise Burwood swindled 750,000 pounds from the victim over a period of six years, roughly 900,000 euros. The victim is a woman of 99. She has since died. The woman held a managerial position in a care home in Flintshire. She forced the resident to transfer the money to her. Burwood also used that money to buy a car and a camper, and ensured she became owner of the house of the very elderly woman. Camper and car bought During a hearing by the British regulator of nursing care (NMC) it emerged that the victim no longer had family and was vulnerable after a fall. She was dependent on Burwood for social contact. The two knew each other before the woman moved into the care home. According to the regulator, Burwood abused her position of trust and power. For example, she persuaded the victim to pay 29,000 pounds for a car and a camper so they could go on trips together. Money was also reportedly spent on renovating Burwood's house. She claimed this was done so the woman could continue living with her if there were a new corona outbreak. But according to the regulator, the renovation had already been paid for before there had been any corona lockdown in the United Kingdom. 'Blackmail' The nurse was caught out when the bank blocked the account of the very elderly woman, due to concerns about high spending. Burwood tried to lift that block by going to the bank with the victim. Staff say the woman was "nearly blackmailed" there and forced to unblock her own account. No prison sentence Burwood will not go to prison for her actions. The police carried out an investigation, but the victim indicated she did not want to take further steps. She saw Burwood as a friend and believed she had learned from her mistakes. The regulator NMC has, however, suspended Burwood for life, meaning she can no longer work as a nurse. NMC speaks of "serious misconduct" by Burwood and calls her actions "morally reprehensible".

title: Dead woman in home in Beek en Donk, man (56) arrested
lead: In the Brabant village of Beek en Donk, near Helmond, a dead woman was found in a house at 02.00 hours. She is a 50-year-old woman who lived in Tilburg. The <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> assumes she died as a result of a crime. The police have arrested a 56-year-old man on suspicion of involvement in her death. The man is in custody and is being questioned, writes Omroep Brabant . Nothing has been made public yet about the relationship between the man and the woman. The police are conducting an investigation at the home: Images show that the glass panels of the front door are broken. According to the regional broadcaster, this was caused by the officers who entered the house overnight.

title: New setback for Ukraine: Trump puts sanctions against Russia on hold
lead: US President Trump is putting a sanctions package against Russia on hold for now. Those sanctions had already been adopted a month ago and signed by himself, but according to Trump it is in the interest of the United States to refrain from them now. It concerns the so-called Graham Act, named after the recently deceased senator Lindsey Graham. He campaigned for years for sanctions against Russia. The sanctions package included, among other things, that import duties of up to 100 percent could be imposed on the five largest importers of Russian oil or natural gas, such as China, India and Turkey. The sanctions also targeted Russian banks, officials and the shadow fleet. Trump signed it after a majority in Congress had also voted for the Graham package. It was seen as the largest form of support for Ukraine since Trump's return to the White House. In a decree, Trump now writes that the penalties will not come after all, at least for now. "I refrain from imposing the sanctions, restrictions and obligations laid down in the Graham Act." Although the act was already signed, the president claims entitlement to an exemption. That would be "in the national interest of the United States". Diesel deal Over the past week Trump has increasingly sought rapprochement with Russia. For example, last week he concluded a diesel deal with Russian President Putin. By his own account, this was to bring down global fuel prices. That drew global criticism from, among others, <entity id="person:rob-jetten">premier Jetten</entity>, who stated that Trump is thereby filling the Russian war chest. The US president also clashed with Ukrainian President Zelensky, who feels betrayed by the diesel agreement. Trump, for his part, stated that it was time for a new Ukrainian president.
