lead: To prevent further riots in the Amsterdam neighbourhood of Floradorp, mayor <entity id="person:femke-halsema">Femke Halsema</entity> has introduced camera surveillance. Since the municipality rejected the annual bonfire on New Year's Eve last week, unrest has reigned in the neighbourhood. There were riots and the riot police (ME) had to be deployed several times. The cameras will remain in place until 7 January. Residents were angry last week when they heard that their alternative plan for a smaller bonfire on New Year's Eve was not allowed to go ahead. Last year the New Year's Eve bonfire was banned for safety reasons. Therefore residents proposed to light a smaller fire in an open container this year. According to the fire service this would still be too dangerous. Halsema adopted the fire service's advice, which led to anger among residents. People then gathered on the street and started several small fires. They also pelted the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> with fireworks. On Monday things went wrong again in the neighbourhood and the mobile unit (ME) had to be deployed. Two suspects were arrested. Feelings of insecurity: The regional broadcaster NH writes that the cameras have been placed both in and around the neighbourhood. Residents are said to feel unsafe. "The incidents pose a threat to public order", the municipality writes. "As a result, feelings of insecurity have arisen among residents. There is also fear of further disturbances in this area." The police said earlier that residents were worried. Officers and youth workers have been present in the neighbourhood in recent days to make contact with residents.

title: Woman gives birth to child on moving train in the city of Groningen
lead: In a train in the city of Groningen, a woman gave birth to a child this morning. Het Dagblad van het Noorden spoke with a witness who boarded at Groningen Europapark station around 08.00. The train had barely left when the witness heard a woman groaning. "Then two loud screams and a sort of 'klonk', the sound of a bag with two bottles falling," the newspaper quotes her as saying. "Someone shouted: 'There's a baby on the ground!' And that was true, there was a little baby on the ground." Fellow passengers called the emergency services and asked whether there was a doctor on the train. Someone said: "The baby is okay, I think that was to reassure the mother," the witness said. The train was met at Groningen's main station by emergency services, who took the mother and child with them. Transport operator Arriva does not want to say, out of concern for the privacy of those involved, how they are doing. Dagblad van het Noorden heard from a second witness that they are doing well.

title: Don't Stop Believin': popular musical series Glee makes a comeback on Disney+
lead: The musical series Glee is definitively getting a comeback. This is confirmed by the American streaming services Disney+ and Hulu. The series was a big hit between 2009 and 2015. Creator Ryan Murphy already said last month that he had written a new script. In the series, which is set at a school in Ohio, students set up a new choir: New Directions . Under the guidance of their teacher, they try to become successful with the choir. Meanwhile, the choir members face, among other things, romance, bullying and all kinds of personal problems. Of course, there is also a lot of singing in the musical series. For example, the Glee version of Don't Stop Believin' by Journey grew into an international hit. In the Netherlands, the series aired on RTL 5. Last month, Murphy told the TV programme Entertainment Tonight that he has been in contact with ten members of the original cast. "It was very heartwarming and they had many questions, but they were all very enthusiastic." Deceased actors More than ten years after the last season, three actors from the series have died. One of the lead actors, Cory Monteith, died in 2013 of an overdose of alcohol and drugs. Mark Salling took his own life in 2018, just before he was due to stand trial for possession of child pornography. Naya Rivera drowned in 2020 while swimming with her young son. Much is still unclear about the precise storyline and cast of the comeback. The details are still being kept secret. 113 Are you thinking about suicide or worried about someone? Talking about it helps and can be done anonymously via the chat at www.113.nl or by phone on 113 or 0800-0113.

title: Arab parties in Israel could play a key role in the elections, but cooperation is sensitive
lead: The Arab parties in Israel could play a decisive role in forming a government without Prime Minister Netanyahu after next week's elections. Jewish opposition leaders would then have to be willing to work with them. Such cooperation has been extra sensitive since the Hamas terror attack of 7 October 2023. Still, the United Arab List is making an effort. At a small parking lot in the center of the Bedouin town of Lakiya in the south of Israel, residents are getting ready for a campaign gathering of the United Arab List. Some banners are quickly being hung on trees and cars. Party leader Mansour Abbas could arrive at any moment. The Palestinian residents here have very different concerns than their Jewish fellow citizens. "We have suffered enormously under this racist government," says Ismail Abli. "Our homes are being demolished and we are dealing with violence." Ayoub al-Baz points to the rise in crime within the Arab community. "This government has failed to deal with this." 'Your vote can make a difference' The banners are up now and a few cars have just been quickly moved aside. Mansour Abbas arrives ten minutes later than planned. Some of the roughly thirty residents who came to the gathering sit down on white plastic chairs. "Your vote for the United Arab List can make the difference," Abbas calls out. He does not use the microphone. "Your vote can bring down this racist government." Abbas hopes that he will end up in the coalition and that the situation for Palestinian residents in Israel can be improved. But most Jewish opposition leaders rule out cooperation with Arab parties. "All political leaders, both in the coalition and in the opposition, say one thing before the elections and then do something completely different afterwards," Abbas tells the NOS. "We are citizens with full political rights. We will not accept anyone excluding us." Arik Rudnitzky of the think tank Israel Democracy Institute explains that the Jewish opposition leaders are taking into account the sensitive and tense situation within the Jewish community after the terror of 7 October. "A majority of the population still lives with that trauma." Still, the Arab parties could be an important partner for the Jewish opposition leaders in defeating Prime Minister Netanyahu. The Knesset, the Israeli parliament, has 120 seats. A majority coalition therefore requires at least 61 seats. According to recent polls, neither Netanyahu with his coalition nor the opposition bloc reaches that majority. With the seats of the United Arab List added, that picture could change. The other Arab parties, united in the Joint List, do not want to be part of the new government themselves. But they do not rule out supporting a government from outside, by voting along on certain bills. Rudnitzky thinks that excluding Arab parties is mainly political campaigning. He points to 2021, when Mansour Abbas's party joined the coalition of Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid. There was also a lot of resistance to cooperation with an Arab party then, but in the end that coalition came about anyway. Turnout becomes crucial According to Rudnitzky, turnout among Palestinian residents of Israel in particular plays an important role. "If the United Arab List wins 7 or 8 seats, for example, it is hard to imagine how Jewish parties could keep ruling out considering them as a potential coalition partner." The big question is whether Abbas will manage to get enough people to the ballot box. Turnout among Palestinian Israelis was relatively low in previous elections. It often hovers around 50 percent. Nationally, turnout at the last elections was 70 percent. Still, the party leader thinks it will be different this time. "We see more enthusiasm and a stronger will among residents to go out and vote." The residents who came to the gathering agree. "The discriminatory policy of this government has created social awareness," says Ismail Abli. "People now realise that if they remain politically indifferent, Israel could ultimately end up with governments that are even more extreme than this one." Ayoub al-Baz thinks the same. He refers to the far-right ministers Ben-Gvir and Smotrich from the current government. "We are more aware of the situation and more motivated to vote and to remove them from their posts."

title: Meta fined 25 billion dollars after lying about user data
lead: Meta, the parent company of Facebook, must pay 25 billion dollars because it misled users about how and by whom their data is used. Facebook knew that other parties could access user data, but denied this. The judge in the American state of New Mexico has therefore imposed the billion-dollar fine on the social media company today. The ruling follows a case surrounding the scandal at data company Cambridge Analytica. That company misused tens of millions of user data via Facebook to help President Trump in the 2016 elections. The data made it possible to place targeted advertisements that Americans saw. It was the biggest violation of privacy in Facebook's history. Although the social network knew about this, it hardly took any action. Cambridge Analytica shut down in 2018 because of this scandal. Violations of legislation. Years later, the state of New Mexico sued Facebook. In September a jury ruled that Meta had made misleading claims about access to user data. The tech company committed more than 43 million violations of consumer legislation in New Mexico. Meta's money is intended to go to education in the American state.

title: Offices of dissolved far-right group in EU Parliament searched
lead: Searches were carried out this morning at offices of the European Parliament in Strasbourg and Brussels. The raids are part of the ongoing investigation into possible misuse of EU money by the dissolved far-right group Identity and Democracy (ID). This group was dissolved in 2024 and succeeded by Patriots for Europe (PfE). According to PfE, searches were carried out in administrative offices of the dissolved ID group. The PfE leadership says in a statement that the new group is completely unconnected to the investigation. The investigation is being carried out by EPPO, the European <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity>. This body confirmed to NOS that searches were carried out on "the premises of the European Parliament in France and Belgium", but gave no further details. Raids last summer as well. Last summer, raids were carried out in the same investigation in Spain, France, Italy and Belgium. Members of the ID group are accused of improperly using more than 4 million euros of community money. For example, companies linked to confidants are said to have received contracts without the tendering procedures. The fraud is said to have taken place between 2019 and 2024. During that period, the Dutch PVV, the French Rassemblement National and the Italian Lega were among the members of ID. Le Pen conviction. French presidential candidate Marine Le Pen has been convicted of fraud involving EU money. Initially she was not allowed to run in next year's elections, but that penalty was reversed on appeal last July. Le Pen remains guilty of illegally funnelling millions of European money into her party's coffers. That happened between 2006 and 2014, when she was a member of the European Parliament. Le Pen has consistently dismissed the case against her as a politically motivated trial.

title: Pope Leo does not need further treatment after cancer operation
lead: Pope Leo XIV does not need any further treatment after his operation last week. His doctors state this in a statement to the Vatican. Tissue was taken from the Pope for research. The structure, composition and any abnormalities of his body tissues were examined. The research showed that his illness remained limited to the original site. The 71-year-old Leo was found to have lung cancer during an operation last week. He was operated on for a small lung nodule, which was discovered during a medical check-up. The nodule proved to be malignant. The operation was successful and without complications. The lower part of the Pope's right lung was removed. Mass in hospital His recovery is also going well. Last week it was already clear that the Pope can eat well again and that he is doing breathing exercises. Last Friday the Pope celebrated a mass in the hospital and distributed communion. During the mass, Pope Leo thanked the healthcare workers for the care they provide "for vulnerable patients, and especially for what they have done and continue to do for him". Last Saturday he was discharged from the hospital. By then, the results of blood tests and scans of his chest were already good, and the Pope was in a "suitable" overall clinical condition.

title: Former Northern Irish politician suspected of raping woman in British House of Commons
lead: London police are investigating the suspected rape of a woman in the buildings of the British parliament. The suspect is a former leader of the Northern Irish party DUP, Jeffrey Donaldson (63), who sat in the House of Commons between 2015 and 2024. Last week he was already sentenced to fifteen years in prison for rape and sexual abuse of two girls between 1985 and 2008. The new suspicion concerns the accusation of rape in 2016. The alleged victim is a Northern Irish woman whom Donaldson showed around the House of Commons. "Donaldson introduced her to influential people, took her to a dinner in the members' restaurant and then took her to the DUP offices in the same building", writes Belfast Telegraph . Initially indecent assault The newspaper already reported on this in July. At that time the accusation was that Donaldson had tried to kiss her and that he had placed his hand on her skirt. The police now tell the newspaper and the BBC that the suspicion is that he raped her. The case was initially investigated by the police in Northern Ireland, but on 13 October it was transferred to the London police, because the rape is said to have taken place there. The London police say the investigation is at an early stage. Donaldson has not yet been arrested or questioned. Wife In the case for which Donaldson was sentenced last week, his wife was also found guilty by a jury. She helped her husband with the rape and the abuse of the two minors. The court still has to pass the sentence she receives. Donaldson and his wife are appealing against the convictions.

title: Iconic Apekop train (now really) runs its last passenger service
lead: For years the Mat '64, also known as Apekop, was a symbol of the train in the Netherlands. Today the iconic train ran a regular passenger service for the last time. In fact, the train had already said goodbye to the track in 2016. At that time the NS removed the last train sets from the timetable. Last year the Apekop unexpectedly returned to the route between Amersfoort and Ede-Barneveld Zuid. Operator Keolis had a shortage of trains because part of the existing rolling stock was being refurbished. The company therefore rented a Mat '64 from Stichting 2454CRW, a group of volunteers who manage and maintain old trains. When the trains returned to the timetable, this led to enthusiastic reactions: Today the Apekop departed at 12.25 for its last regular trip from Barneveld Zuid. At the end of this year the foundation will take the museum train back under its own management. The Mat '64 (Materieel '64) was the last train type built in the Netherlands. The first units ran on the tracks in 1961. At its peak, hundreds ran, mainly as stopping trains. The trains got the nickname 'Apekop' because of their striking nose. The design with a rounded nose looks somewhat like the Hondekop, which is ten years older.

title: Criticism of Republican who uses opponent's mother in campaign ad
lead: The battle between Republicans and Democrats in the United States has reached a new low. Republican gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy in the state of Ohio is under fire for deploying the biological mother of his Democratic opponent Amy Acton to smear her. In the video, Donna Arthur, Acton's mother, accuses her daughter, among other things, of being a liar and of having lied about her entire life. Arthur also says that the 60-year-old Acton needs help and calls on people not to vote for her. The video lasts one minute and was first shared on social media by a local political blogger. The campaign ad went online yesterday and is drawing criticism from both Republican and Democratic quarters, because Acton is being confronted with her painful youth. The gubernatorial candidate has in fact had no contact with her biological mother since her youth. Rape Acton was removed from her mother together with her brother at the age of 12 due to severe abuse, neglect and sexual abuse. She was reportedly raped by her stepfather. Acton's campaign team has shared court documents with American media confirming her account. The documents, which were also viewed by news agency Associated Press (AP), show that Acton's stepfather was charged in 1978 with raping Acton. According to the documents, the rapes took place between 1976 and 1978. The report was filed by Acton's biological father. For a time it was unclear who had financed the ad. The video did not carry the required "paid for" notice showing who paid for the advertisement. Acton quickly pointed to Ramaswamy. The campaign team of the 41-year-old Ramaswamy confirmed today that it is behind the controversial video. The Republican has let it be known that he will set aside 4 million dollars to spread the ad further, despite the criticism. Even before Ramaswamy confirmed the video, his spokesperson told American media that he did not know what had happened between Acton and her biological mother. "But we do know that Amy Acton is a pathological liar. She has a serious problem with the truth." Political gain Acton reacted furiously to the ad. "I am not going to normalise someone who claims that my youth is just something I am complaining about." On social media, Acton shared a statement from her brother in which he accuses Ramaswamy of using his sister's sexual abuse for his own political gain. "This desperate, disgusting attack reveals exactly who Vivek Ramaswamy is at his core: a miserable man, who is willing to hurt anyone as long as he gets what he wants", says brother Philip Stearns. 'Stop complaining' The video was widely shared on social media, including by the son of President Trump, Donald Trump Jr., and far-right conspiracy theorist Laura Loomer. Prominent Republicans such as Nikki Haley and Meghan McCain criticised the campaign ad and considered it to go too far. Vice President JD Vance warned Republicans to "stop complaining" about the ad. During a campaign visit to Ohio he said that he is "disgusted" by the criticism from Republican quarters and that "politics is a tough world". He called on his fellow Republicans to focus on winning the midterm elections. It is not known whether the campaign ad will cost Ramaswamy votes. According to American polls, it is a neck-and-neck race in Ohio.

title: Still websites unreachable after leak, international problems too
lead: Websites are still unreachable after being taken offline as a precaution. This happened after a leak in the programming language PHP. For example, the website overheid.nl is still unreachable, as is the site of Meld Misdaad Anoniem. The sites of 113 and Centrum Seksueel Geweld were offline until late, but became reachable again during the night. A spokesperson for the <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-biza">Binnenlandse Zaken</entity> ministry says it is not yet clear when overheid.nl will be available again. Some sites take longer to update their systems and are therefore not yet online. More than a hundred municipalities, provinces and water boards use the council system Notubiz for distributing official letters. That organisation's website is online, but not every component can be used by municipalities or provinces. Official documents from, among others, the municipalities <entity id="org:gemeente-s-gravenhage">Den Haag</entity>, <entity id="org:gemeente-almere">Almere</entity>, Breda, <entity id="org:gemeente-haarlem">Haarlem</entity>, Den Bosch and Delft, and of the provinces <entity id="org:provincie-overijssel">Overijssel</entity>, <entity id="org:provincie-gelderland">Gelderland</entity> and <entity id="org:provincie-fryslan">Friesland</entity>, cannot be viewed. NotuBiz wants to test tonight first whether the updates have been applied properly and expects all pages to be available again tomorrow morning. Update A programming language is a language with which programmers can build websites, apps and software. Around 70 percent of all websites worldwide use the programming language PHP or a variation of it. That is why so many websites went offline today, including internationally. At 16.00 yesterday afternoon the organisation behind the programming language PHP carried out a security update that users could install. As a result, websites could start up safely again. Many sites are back online, but for some others that is not the case. Internationally too, websites went offline as a precaution. Besides the Netherlands, government websites in Belgium, Finland, Germany and France could not be used. For Belgium and France that is still the case. After the American organisation behind PHP, the PHP Foundation, announced yesterday that it would carry out a security update today, hackers seized on the announcement to locate the vulnerability and spread information about it. The information could have been misused; malicious people could have broken into websites using the programming language to steal customer data. In 2024 there were already signs that something was wrong with the PHP programming language. But other, more concrete problems overshadowed the signs, the PHP Foundation writes on its own site. Then the first vulnerability was found on 11 August by researchers from the security company Calif in cooperation with OpenAI. A special AI model was used for that. The second vulnerability was discovered on 24 August by security company Wiz, which is owned by Google. No indication of misuse According to the PHP Foundation, there are for now no signals that the vulnerabilities in the programming language have led to misuse of companies via their websites. The Dutch <entity id="org:nationaal-cyber-security-centrum">NCSC</entity> and the American CISA, both specialised in cybersecurity, confirm this. They say they have seen no active misuse of the vulnerability.

title: US withdraws part of embassy staff from Saudi Arabia after deadly Houthi attacks
lead: The American Department of State has ordered part of the diplomatic staff and their family members to leave Saudi Arabia. This concerns 'non-essential personnel' of the American embassy in the capital Riyadh and the consulates in the country. This decision follows a series of deadly attacks in the country by the Iran-backed Houthi rebels from neighbouring Yemen. There is fear that the conflict that flared up again this summer will escalate further. Civilian casualties Saudi Arabia supports the internationally recognised government in Yemen and is therefore targeted by the Yemeni Houthi fighters. Recently the Houthis have stepped up the violence, by their own account as retaliation for attacks on Houthi targets in Yemen. In a new travel advice the American Department of State says: "Iran-backed Houthis are carrying out hostilities against Saudi Arabia, including attacks on civilian airports and other critical infrastructure. This has led to civilian casualties and serious disruptions to travel. There is a risk that these hostilities will quickly escalate beyond the immediate area." According to American government sources of news agency Reuters, family members of embassy staff in other Gulf states will also have to leave. The ministry said nothing about that. International airport Among other things, airports in Saudi Arabia and power plants were targeted by the Houthis this month, with deaths as a result. For example, last night at an attack on an airfield in Dammam one person died and eight others were injured. The international airport in Riyadh was also hit this month. News agency AP reports that yesterday planes again took off and landed at the airport in the capital Riyadh. Major airlines such as Lufthansa and Air France have for now cancelled their flights to Riyadh until mid-November. Saudi airlines did operate flights yesterday. British fighter jets This week it became known that the United Kingdom is coming to Saudi Arabia's aid. The British Air Force will protect Saudi airspace against Houthi attacks. The country is sending, among other things, several Typhoon fighter jets. According to the British Ministry of Defence, this is a mission with a defensive purpose: the fighter jets will not carry out attacks. The support follows a request from the Saudi government. The United Kingdom has for some time been giving Saudi Arabia defensive support in the fight against the Houthis. For example, Saudi combat aircraft can use British tanker aircraft to refuel in the air.

title: North Korea warns South Korea: propaganda loudspeakers at the border almost ready
lead: North Korea says it has loudspeakers ready along the entire border with South Korea within a few days. That announcement was made by Kim Yo-jong, sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong-un. The threat of new propaganda speakers seems to undo the progress the South Korean president has made in reducing tensions with the neighboring country. Reducing those tensions was an election promise of Lee Jae-myung, who has been president of South Korea since June last year. K-pop and crying animals: Until early August 2025, loudspeakers stood on both sides of the border, used for psychological warfare. From South Korea, criticism of the North Korean regime and K-pop music blared. In response, sounds of crying animals and banging gongs came from the North Korean speakers. To reduce tensions, South Korea switched off the loudspeakers on 11 June last year. A day later North Korea did the same. Then South Korea began removing the speakers at the border in August. North Korea again followed that example. Landmines: Now those speakers are partly returning and tensions have risen again. Kim responded with her statement to remarks by a special adviser to President Lee. This adviser on defense policy had accused North Korea of planting landmines that injured South Korean soldiers, and had called on the country not to escalate further with loudspeaker broadcasts. Kim spoke of "new countermeasures" along the entire border and added that North Korea will continue strengthening the border. North Korea's warning does not necessarily mean the loudspeakers will be switched back on, says Lim Eul-chul of Kyungnam University in Seoul to news agency Reuters. However, he says this raises the question for the South Korean <entity id="org:regering">regering</entity> of whether the rapprochement policy should be continued.

title: Three dead in storms and flooding in southern France
lead: Three people have died and one person has been injured in heavy rainfall and flooding near Marseille in southern France. The authorities of the Bouches-du-Rhône department announced this. The storm hit the region on Tuesday. According to the regional authorities, the water level has risen to "unprecedented levels". The municipalities of Saint-Martin-de-Crau and Arles have been hit by a power outage since the storm, which may last a long time, the regional government warns. In addition, several roads in the region remain closed and rail traffic is still disrupted in some places. There are also faults in the telephone network, making communication difficult in areas without power. In Saint-Martin-de-Crau, 250 people have been housed in emergency shelters. Drowned Among the victims who died, according to the newspaper La Provence, are an 86-year-old woman and a 26-year-old woman. They reportedly drowned in a basement in Lançon-Provence. In addition, a 75-year-old man died in Saint-Mitre-les-Remparts. According to the mayor of the town, he was swept away by the current and his body was found later that morning. The authorities speak of "considerable material damage". An assessment of this is still ongoing.

title: Number of new businesses rises sharply, over 8 in 10 are zzp'ers
lead: The <entity id="org:zbo-kamer-van-koophandel">Kamer van Koophandel</entity> (KVK) recorded the number of startups in the Netherlands in the third quarter of this year rising by over 15 percent compared with the same period last year. This is the strongest increase in years. Mainly the number of sole proprietorships increased. Of all 62.395 'starters', as the KVK calls them, over eight in ten are zzp'ers. The number of self-employed people without staff is therefore 20 percent higher than a year earlier. "Despite discussions about bogus self-employment and measures to curb the use of zzp'ers, this form of entrepreneurship remains an important part of the economy", the KVK writes. Bogus self-employment occurs when someone is a zzp'er on paper but in practice does the same work as an employee. Bankruptcies At the same time, fewer businesses stopped. In the third quarter, 36.610 businesses were dissolved, 4,3 percent fewer than a year earlier. The number of bankruptcies rose slightly, by just under one percent. In total, on 1 October over 2,6 million businesses were registered with the KVK. That is 1,5 percent more than a year ago. For ten years politics has struggled with the zzp rules. The new Zelfstandigenwet, due to take effect in 2028, is meant to put an end to this. Five questions and answers on this:

title: Tensions rise between the Philippines and China over the South China Sea
lead: The Philippines and China are on a collision course over claims to island groups and reefs in the South China Sea. China claims almost the entire area and regularly has collisions with neighbouring countries that also claim parts of it on the basis of the law of the sea. Manila and Beijing have been quarrelling for years over the Spratly Islands and Scarborough Shoal. Now a new potential conflict zone seems to be emerging: the Batanes Islands, the northernmost province of the Philippines. The location is strategic, about 200 kilometres from Taiwan. Diplomatically, tensions are also rising, after statements by the Chinese ambassador last week. Ambassador Jing Quan said China could "easily win" a war, which Filipinos see as a threat. Quan has since been called in by the Philippine Department of Foreign Affairs. Claims to the Batanes Islands This summer a group of Chinese scientists concluded that the Batanes Islands "are a natural geographical extension of the island of Taiwan". Beijing sees Taiwan as part of China and is therefore now also claiming the Batanes Islands. The islands are not particularly impressive. Only three of the ten are inhabited, with just over 19,000 residents. Among them are mainly fishers, farmers who grow sweet potatoes and some hotel owners serving the roughly 13,000 tourists per year. It is mainly the location that makes a geopolitical impression: in the Luzon Strait, which would give the Chinese navy direct access to the Pacific Ocean, military experts say. The Chinese scientific claim was immediately rejected by the Philippines. According to the Department of Foreign Affairs, sovereignty over the Batanes Islands is "settled and the discussion is closed". Filipino historians stress that the islands have been part of the archipelago since the 18th century, when the Spanish colonised them. In 2016 the Permanent Court of Arbitration in <entity id="org:gemeente-s-gravenhage">Den Haag</entity> rejected Chinese claims in the South China Sea, after the Philippines had brought a case. China refuses to recognise the ruling. There is no legal basis for China to claim the Batanes Islands, but by raising it, the claim can start to sound legitimate, says Harvard scholar of Taiwan Studies Felix Brender to Channel News Asia. "The danger is that repetition makes Philippine territory sound disputed." Diplomatic row Meanwhile the diplomatic outbursts are increasing. Philippine Defence Secretary Teodoro called China a "regional troublemaker". Early this summer China already put Teodoro on its sanctions list, because of earlier statements. In response, Ambassador Quan said: "If China were to use military force, we could easily win. But China loves peace, which is why we do not choose violence." The Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs also chipped in, saying "the Philippines should curb such irresponsible behaviour by those politicians". The Filipinos were shocked and, by their own account, deployed the strongest diplomatic tool available. The ambassador has been summoned by President Marcos. "To me this sounded like a threat, and not a very diplomatic statement," the president said. "I think it deserves a discussion between the ambassador and me." The meeting has yet to take place. But Ambassador Jing Quan now denies that his words were meant as a threat. Still, it is no coincidence that China is speaking out so firmly. Since Marcos took office, his government has moved closer to the US. Three years ago his government gave the Americans access to three military bases in northern Luzon. That is the largest island of the Philippines, and the island closest to the Batanes Islands and therefore Taiwan. His army also holds military exercises with Japan in that area. That is a thorn in China's side. Over the past year relations between China and Japan have cooled sharply, after Japanese Prime Minister Takaichi said that a Chinese attack on Taiwan "could create a situation that threatens Japan's survival". But China is also steadily expanding its military exercises and activities in the South China Sea. Last month the Chinese navy and air force held exercises around Scarborough Shoal, which drew fierce criticism from the Philippines and the US.

In the latest episode of Het Misdaadbureau, Maaike Timmerman talks with director Joost van der Valk. His documentary Motorbendes is about the rise and fall of motorcycle gangs. Timmerman also speaks with Niels Huisman of the <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> and with former police chief Peter Graafland, who conducted research into the Hells Angels.

title: Rotterdam Marathon drops lottery for allocating starting passes
lead: The Rotterdam Marathon is abandoning the lottery system for allocating starting passes for the upcoming edition on 11 April 2027. Pre-registration will remain, but unlike last year it is free, the organisation reports.

title: Vote approaching, but support for the cabinet's tax plans is far off
lead: The opposition objects, among other things, to billions in tax increases for workers. In <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Kamer</entity> there was no sign of a majority yet on the first day of the debate.

title: Hello government. Stop running breathlessly from one poll to the next on the leash of Maurice de Hond
State Secretary Erkens wants to end unstunned slaughter: 'Does not fit our idea of animal welfare'
lead: The debate over unstunned slaughter is flaring up again this Animal Day. VVD State Secretary Silvio Erkens for Animal Welfare tells RTL Nieuws in an interview about animal welfare that it is very awkward that other countries such as Belgium already have a ban, but our country does not yet. This month the Party for the Animals will send a private member's bill to the House to ban unstunned slaughter.

title: Owner who became the target of the Vlaardingen hairdresser war has lost his shop: 'I have nothing left'
lead: Stones through the window, paint on the shop and even explosions. For a year Baz Hair Salon 4 was the target of the Vlaardingen hairdresser war. The owner has now lost his shop. "I've been ruined."

title: Cold but sunny day: real autumn weather only arrives at the weekend
lead: It is a beautiful day for the autumn holiday: this morning and this afternoon the sun shines brightly. From tomorrow we switch to an increasingly unsettled type of weather. Especially from Friday onward it is regularly soaking wet, and along the coast there is sometimes a lot of wind, with a chance of severe gusts.

title: How do you know what is going on in 'the undercurrent'?
lead: When a team is not functioning, when leadership is not working or when a change gets stuck, people often say: we need to look at the undercurrent.

title: In this play about the housing crisis, she wants a parquet floor and he wants laminate: 'There is also room for love and humour'
'Since I stopped drinking I have so much more energy: suddenly I feel like clearing out the attic'
Sophie Hermans gives patients with post-acute infection syndromes a slap in the face
lead: From apologies to a slap in the face for PAIS patients in the Netherlands

title: Two arrests after police pelted during fresh unrest in Amsterdam-Noord
lead: Two people were arrested on Monday evening in the Amsterdam neighbourhood of Floradorp. It was again restless there. Fireworks were set off and fires were started. Police were also pelted with stones and glassware.

title: Doctors in England have ethical objections to Palantir's software, and so do patients
lead: Making English healthcare more efficient was a prestigious job for the American tech company Palantir. Now the Labour government is under pressure to stop the multimillion-euro contract. "Distrust of Palantir undermines general support for sharing data."

title: Vote on secession stirs Canadian pride in Alberta: 'We are angry that this is even on the agenda'
lead: Voters in Alberta vote on Monday in a referendum on whether the western Canadian province should pursue independence. A fierce separatist movement managed to force the vote, but has provoked a determined counter-reaction. "This is no game."

title: Build. Fly. Adjust course. How SpaceX is working on the largest spaceship ever
lead: SpaceX is investing heavily in the giant Starship rocket, with which the American company wants to conquer space. For the rest of the sector, that focus has a dark side.

title: Neck-and-neck race ahead of Israeli elections: former army chief Gadi Eisenkot hopes to succeed Netanyahu
lead: Netanyahu's main rival in the upcoming elections is former army chief Gadi Eisenkot. In Israel, supporters and analysts call him the 'anti-Bibi'. When it comes to the Palestinians, he will make little difference.

title: Pastor may have known of sexual abuse by his own daughter: church in Elspeet in crisis
lead: A woman (39) from Elspeet is being prosecuted for sexual abuse of at least one underage girl. She is a former conductor of the Reformed Congregation in Elspeet. The matter is dividing the church community.

title: Inform buyers and new tenants about heavy power connections, advises the Woonbond
lead: Make it mandatory to inform home buyers and new tenants in advance about what type of power connection is in their new home. That is what the Woonbond says, in a response to the news from regulator <entity id="org:zbo-autoriteit-consument-en-markt">ACM</entity> this week. Parties in <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> embrace the idea.

title: Great discontent among VVD voters over cabinet's concession to the left, PRO voters pleased with package of adjustments
lead: VVD voters react angrily to the U-turn the cabinet is making. They respond with incomprehension to the tax on more savers and say the gesture towards PRO is massively unacceptable. PRO voters, on the other hand, are pleased with the cabinet's adjustments.

title: Many websites taken offline due to security vulnerabilities. 'This is serious'

lead: MANCHESTER (ANP/RTR) - Former Manchester United manager Erik ten Hag has spoken harshly, four years after Cristiano Ronaldo left the club, about the conduct of the Portuguese star player. The Dutch coach was not happy with Ronaldo's fitness and preparation.

title: The US resistance to the ICC runs deep. As the 'policeman of the world', they believe they deserve reward rather than punishment
lead: Already in 2002, <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">de Senaat</entity> decided to take on the International Criminal Court militarily if necessary. Diplomats look back in history and have advice for now: "You say: we know what you want. Then you say 'no'. And keep saying 'no'."

title: Prime Minister Jetten and his partner Nicolás Keenan are expecting a child. "This involves high-tech surrogacy"
lead: The surrogate is a Dutch woman named Lisa. She is an acquaintance of the prime minister and Keenan. It is explicitly not commercial surrogacy, D66 writes. The egg donor is also an acquaintance of the couple.

title: Woman gives birth in a moving train in Groningen, passengers come to help
lead: A woman gave birth on Monday morning in a moving train in Groningen. Carrier Arriva confirms this to RTL Nieuws. The woman was on her way to the hospital for a check-up when her waters broke, Dagblad van het Noorden writes.

title: Tackling healthcare fraud requires cooperation and setting limits
lead: An effective approach to healthcare fraud requires cooperation with professional care providers, setting standards and checking compliance with them. This is stated in the framework for action 'Municipal grip on healthcare fraud: Five tasks for local government to reduce healthcare fraud', which is being presented today during the semester session 'Insight into Subversion' in <entity id="org:gemeente-utrecht">Utrecht</entity>. 'Continuously look for signs of healthcare fraud and intervene when necessary.'

title: Fled victims of childcare benefits scandal want to return to the Netherlands
lead: A considerable number of victims of the childcare benefits scandal who left for abroad out of fear of the <entity id="org:belastingdienst">Belastingdienst</entity> want to return to the Netherlands. Since 2022, 229 families have returned with help from the Support Team Abroad (OTB); 371 families are now in a return process. But the return to the Netherlands is a bumpy road. 'It's a case of crying with your cap on', says victim Karima Ouadid, who herself moved to Germany.

lead: European plans to reduce dependence on non-European technology companies do not go far enough, according to Dutch municipalities and provinces. The proposed Cloud and AI Development Act (CADA) should set stricter requirements for sovereign cloud services. VNG and IPO also warn that building more data centres in Europe does not automatically lead to more digital autonomy.

lead: Once again the number of elderly people dying after a fall has risen: on average 21 per day, according to new figures from the <entity id="org:zbo-centraal-bureau-voor-de-statistiek">CBS</entity>. It is thus the most common non-natural cause of death in our country, while that is not necessarily 'necessary'.

title: Support in the House of Representatives for billion-euro cut still far off, even though the health minister promises the opposition an 'open mind'
lead: The opposition in the House of Representatives wants health minister <entity id="person:sophie-hermans">Sophie Hermans</entity> to take cuts of 10 billion euros from 2028 off the table, but she is not willing to. In his home region of Sauerland, people realise that 'their' Chancellor Merz is having a hard time. There is also impatience. "I want to see concrete results quickly now."

lead: Special board committees are investigating the combining of Elon Musk's two companies.

lead: On WhatsApp, a new type of scam has been circulating in recent days. Users receive a message asking them to vote for a young ballerina. But anyone who does becomes the victim of hackers who take over the account.

title: Avoid the sambal of this brand: 'Tastes stale, as if it has been in the kitchen cupboard for two years'
lead: At the takeaway Chinese you get it as standard in a sachet. Or it sits at home next to the peanut butter in the cupboard. Sambal oelek adds kick to a bland bite and masks a bad taste. But which brand is the very best? Three sambal specialists worked their way through eight jars. "The hotter, the better."

lead: We should not try to explain the rise of AfD by reference to Germany's wartime past, writes Thomas von der Dunk . The Soviet past and discomfort about support for Ukraine are far too relevant for that.

lead: On social media, Saudis emphasised after Houthi attacks on the Riad airport that their lives simply go on. But they are not free to voice their opinions. The disrupted calm in Saudi Arabia is indeed a major economic problem.

lead: According to critics, the way the Dutch government keeps its books leads to too little investment. But an accrual-based system does not provide extra budgetary room: it remains important not to borrow too much.

Whoever understands it may say so. Political reporter Hans van Soest writes weekly about The Hague affairs that concern us all.

lead: The holiday home in Brabant is going on sale, but there is one problem: the woman is bedridden and cannot go to the notary. Estate agent Benthe Vergouwen-Geerts has an unusual solution for this. 'That way, Mr and Mrs can still arrange their affairs themselves'

title: Biodiversity cannot wait 265 years
lead: Wars, geopolitical instability and the explosive rise of AI rightly demand political attention. But they must never be an excuse to postpone action on the climate and biodiversity crises.

lead: Everyone hates the police

title: From 0 to 97 kilometers per hour in less than one second: Elon Musk demonstrates Tesla's rocket car
lead: Tesla CEO Elon Musk demonstrated a prototype of the new Tesla Roadster at a test site in Texas. According to Musk, the car is equipped with cold-gas thrusters from SpaceX, which allow the vehicle to do somersaults among other things and even fly upside down for a short time. Nobody was sitting in the car during the show 'to make sure nobody dies'.

title: Prime Minister Jetten receives President of the European Council Costa

title: Interim review after 250 days of Jordi Cruijff at Ajax: flopped million-euro signings, but also top performers such as Brandt and Tolu
lead: Jordi Cruijff (52) is at the helm this week for 250 days. The outlines and consequences of his way of working are becoming clearer. What stands out so far? With the tough away game against FC Groningen on the horizon, we draw an interim review of eight conclusions.

title: Cats in Rijksmuseum is a breathtakingly beautiful spectacle, but the story remains paper-thin and slow
lead: The musical Cats has been given a fantastic makeover for the new Dutch version, with the Rijksmuseum as the set and internationally known artworks, and the actors sing and dance superbly. But that does not disguise the fact that this production is at times somewhat boring. Simply because the makers today are not allowed to change anything about the paper-thin storyline and the slow script from the early 1980s.

title: Sparta finally knows the feeling of winning at Het Kasteel again on party evening
lead: On the party evening marking the 110th anniversary of Het Kasteel, Sparta finally managed to win at home again. Bottom-placed Willem II was sent packing 3-2 after an entertaining football evening.

lead: Jan G., het slachtoffer van het geweld in Overasselt in september, is uit Duitsland uitgeleverd.

lead: Dear administrator in public administration, watch out for the 'Pick me FG'.

title: From Trump to Qatar: Infantino's tour shows why the FIFA boss may simply stay put

"My mother once said: go and visit that neighbourhood centre, they can help you there."

lead: Former Northern Irish politician Jeffrey Donaldson was sentenced on Thursday to fifteen years in prison for multiple sexual offences against two female victims. The abuse began when they were seven years old and continued for just over twenty years.

lead: Japan launched a space probe yesterday that is on its way to Phobos and Deimos, the two moons of the planet Mars. The unmanned vehicle is due, among other things, to land on Phobos to collect dust there and bring it back to Earth so scientists can study it. Nothing like this has ever been done before.

title: Earth is warming much more strongly than agreed under current global climate policy
lead: Global warming is far from under control. Worldwide greenhouse gas emissions must fall much faster than countries indicate in their climate plans. That is what the UN organisation UNEP concludes on the eve of another global climate summit, this year in Turkey.

title: No trains all day between Rotterdam and Delft due to arson at the railway
lead: No trains will run between Rotterdam and Delft on Saturday due to arson at the Delfshaven railway bridge, ProRail reports. The disruption began at 2.30 a.m. and is expected to last until the end of the Saturday timetable.

title: PostNL wants extra compensation of 80 million euros for postal delivery
lead: PostNL is seeking government compensation of 80 million euros for the coming year, due to rising costs of legally mandated postal delivery. The delivery service previously also applied for subsidies for 2025 and 2026. A legal procedure is still ongoing regarding these applications.

title: Trump was unaware of Hegseth's plan to livestream execution
lead: US President Donald Trump was not aware of the plans of War Secretary Pete Hegseth to broadcast the execution of shooter Nidal Hasan live. Trump has since put a stop to the plan.

title: Prison sentence for soldier who passed on confidential information for drugs and money
lead: The military chamber of the court on Monday sentenced a 32-year-old soldier from Spijkenisse to two years in prison, of which ten months are suspended. According to the court, the man searched confidential information in police systems for years and partly passed it on in exchange for cocaine and money.

lead: Of course, the Porsche of all Porsches is the 911, the well-known classic from the 1960s that is a dream car for many. But now and then the brand aims higher. The brand has now unveiled the Mission S: a harbinger of a new top model.

lead: They had to close their shop and stood in front of the facade until deep into the night to prevent the place from being wrecked. The half-Dutch Bastien (27) runs a Dutch snack bar on the main street of Bordeaux and was in the middle of the riots on Saturday. "Groups of teenagers were destroying everything and shouting."

lead: Thomas Hogeling weekly considers public opinion. What is being said and, above all, what is not being said? This week: decent spectacle television.

lead: CEO Tim Cook has stepped down, chips have become extremely expensive, the AI applications are lagging: investors have enough reasons to punish Apple. But the tech group remains a stock market darling.

Lead researcher Ewoud Kieft, affiliated with the NIOD, published this week the study on sexual violence in the Dutch internment camps for collaboration suspects 1944-1947. title: A new twist on fraud
lead: The criminals are among us and will not rest until they have squeezed the last cent out of our pockets. In the past they were rogues who came to tidy up your garden for a moment and then demanded a few thousand guilders, now they link your WhatsApp account to their own laptop or phone and plunder your bank account.

title: "Grand, complex and not without danger": Kadir van Lohuizen photographed the energy transition in the North Sea
lead: For his project Nieuwe Energie, photographer and filmmaker Kadir van Lohuizen examined what the energy transition in and around the North Sea looks like. Everything in the photos breathes big, bigger, biggest. "That was quite a challenge: how do I show that scale?"

title: 'Putin only understands the language of muscle, diplomacy has long since gone out the window'
lead: In the podcast Praat mee met AD we discuss one issue every day, and today it is this: Should we pay Russia back in its own coin, or should we remain diplomatic?

title: Jumbo recalls pulled chicken because it may contain raw chicken
lead: Supermarket chain Jumbo is recalling the prepared chicken dish pulled chicken because it was not cooked through as stated on the packaging. Customers are asked not to consume the product.

title: Twenty road deaths and 3950 victims: Amsterdam is not yet making traffic safer
71-year-old man dragged away and killed by 3.5 metre long alligator in Florida
lead: A 71-year-old man was killed on Friday by an alligator more than 3.5 metres long in the American state of Florida. The man was fishing in an area known for its alligator population when the animal dragged him away.

title: Minister of Agriculture: understanding for worried farmer, but 'plans stay in place'
lead: The new nitrogen plans of <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> are causing great gloom among Dutch livestock farmers. As many as 87 percent say that because of the plans they have less confidence in the future of their own farm. Minister of Agriculture Van Essen responds today with understanding for the concerns, but stresses that the plans remain in place.

title: Four years in prison demanded against Doetinchem man for preparing attack on asylum centre
lead: The Public Prosecution Service demanded four years in prison on Tuesday against a 37-year-old man from Doetinchem. He is suspected of preparing an attack on an asylum seekers' centre.

title: Being against abortion belongs in the same list as being against asylum seekers, against climate policy, against LGBTI people and against nice people
AI objections add extra work for municipalities
lead: Municipalities, hospitals and public transport companies are increasingly dealing with objections drafted with the help of artificial intelligence (AI). The texts are generally longer, more legalistic and regularly contain incorrect references to legislation. This causes extra work and delays in handling objections.

title: 'I pick up my spirituality from everywhere, but shouldn't I have to choose?'
Trump drops Russia sanctions and tariffs that Congress had approved
lead: US President Donald Trump is dropping heavy import tariffs on Russian energy. These had been approved by Congress in a law named after the late senator Lindsey Graham. According to Trump, they go against the national interest.

title: Rob Jetten and his partner are expecting a baby: the rules on surrogacy in the Netherlands
lead: The Netherlands is getting a 'first baby': Prime Minister Rob Jetten and his fiancé Nicolás Keenan are expecting a child next year. The couple had already expressed their wish to have children, but finding a surrogate is complicated because of the rules in our country.

title: Sunday does not live up to its name: lots of clouds and rain
lead: Don't expect a bright Sunday today: the sun shows itself little. In the west and north of the country it rains this morning, and this afternoon precipitation follows in the south and centre of the country.

title: Choice for maintenance is right, but not at the expense of our water plan
lead: The state of many Dutch waterways and bridges is nothing to be proud of. It is right that <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> is freeing up money for the large backlog of maintenance. But that this comes at the expense of plans to protect us against drought is asking for new problems, writes political reporter Hans van Soest in this commentary.

title: Another person dies after infection with West Nile virus in the Netherlands
lead: In the Netherlands, another person has died after being infected with the West Nile virus. This is the tenth person this year to die after infection with the virus, the <entity id="org:rijksinstituut-voor-volksgezondheid-en-milieu">Rijksinstituut voor Volksgezondheid en Milieu</entity> reported on Thursday.

title: It is time for a diplomatic post at the Court of Elon
lead: The power of tech billionaires now extends well beyond their companies. It is time for the Netherlands and Europe to adapt their diplomacy accordingly.

title: 'I think it's really cozy that you hear 'tok tok tok' when you come home'
lead: Rein Hazelzet (37) and Sanne Brouwer (39) moved from the Randstad to a village in Gelderland, where they renovated an old parsonage into their dream home. "Everything had to be renovated, only the outer walls and the roof were left standing."

title: The world economy hides its suffering behind a smile
lead: Against all odds, the global economy continues to grow. But the risks of AI, trade conflicts and government debt are piling up.

title: All those different bedrooms, and yet the same nest
lead: For years, photographer Bieke Depoorter travelled around Egypt, Russia and the United States and slept at people's homes. What stands out in particular is the resemblance between the bedrooms; the more or less universal nature of the human sleeping place.

title: Medewerkers van asielinstantie zeggen dat klachten over onveilige situaties onbeantwoord blijven; eisen verandering
lead: Medewerkers van Nederlandse asielcentra die onveilige situaties melden, krijgen binnen het Centraal Orgaan opvang asielzoekers (<entity id="org:zbo-centraal-orgaan-opvang-asielzoekers">COA</entity>) geen reactie en hebben hun klachten voorgelegd aan de Arbeidsinspectie

title: Van Roosmalen & Groenteman still not saved, PowNed has to back out: 'It is a crying shame'
lead: The BNNVara programme Van Roosmalen & Groenteman will definitely not move to broadcaster PowNed. "We really wanted to take it over, but we cannot get the financing sorted. It is a crying shame", says Dominique Weesie, director of PowNed.

title: Con artist Elizabeth Holmes draws full cinemas: 'Film of the year'
lead: The biggest con artist of this century is once again the center of attention. Before she went to prison, tech fraudster Elizabeth Holmes let two documentary makers live with her in her home for a month. America can't stop talking about it.

title: Hundreds of millions in damage in France after riots, new protests announced
lead: The unrest in the large French cities does not appear to be over yet: today demonstrating students are blocking access to the Louvre in Paris. New protests have been announced for next weekend.

title: Deaths in major fire incident at military base in Canada: 'A disaster that almost never happens'
lead: At a military base in the Canadian province of Alberta, an unknown number of people have been killed and injured. Prime Minister Mark Carney wrote on X of 'a serious incident that caused a major fire'.

title: US envoy Witkoff meets Putin in Moscow on Wednesday
Environmental organisations go to court over new Schiphol decision
The city is surrounded, and there are many wounded. 'But reliable information is scarce in Yemen'
lead: The escalating fighting between the Houthis and Saudi Arabia is leading to many deaths, injuries and refugees in Yemen. As director of an anti-landmine organization, the Dutch Mara van der Kamp is trying to get a picture of the situation. "The war has once again become part of everyday life."

title: Who will pick up free agent Luuk de Jong (36) after serious knee injury? 'I feel good, I am fit'
lead: Luuk de Jong is open to a new adventure. The striker has recovered from a knee injury he sustained last year. Since last summer the former international has been a free agent.

title: Prisoners increasingly use drones to smuggle items inside, also a juicy morsel
Thomas Heerma van Voss (36) and Maartje Wortel (43) wrote a novella about a love relationship without major resolutions: 'You can compare it to the game Tetris'
Limoges town hall set on fire during education protests, French police arrest 400 people
Videoland may take over streamer Viaplay, including Formula 1 and darts
lead: Streaming service Viaplay will become property of DPG Media, and will be merged with Videoland. The <entity id="org:zbo-autoriteit-consument-en-markt">Autoriteit Consument en Markt</entity> (ACM) has approved this.

title: The fight for LGBTI acceptance is far from over, including in the Tweede Kamer
Jesse Klaver (Pro): 'The VVD calls a deal with us terrible. Then the base will believe it'
The cork the internet floats on is broken: why the attack on PHP is paralysing half the internet
lead: One website after another is going offline due to vulnerabilities in the programming language PHP. Criminals are said to have already begun their first cyberattacks. It is a disaster, because 70 percent of the internet uses PHP. "This is very big."

title: Nederlandse koningin annuleerde werkbezoek waarbij een Pro-Palestijnse band betrokken was op 7 oktober
lead: Koningin Maxima annuleerde een geplande bezoek aan het Tilburgse muziekpodium Poppodium 013 slechts twee weken voor de datum, een zeldzaam voorval voor de Nederlandse koninklijke familie.

title: Outspoken and concerned: Coos Huijsen, the first openly gay parliamentarian in the world, has died
lead: Fifty years ago Coos Huijsen became the first parliamentarian in the world to publicly come out of the closet. Towards the end of his life he was worried about the waning acceptance of homosexuality.

title: 'It seems as if the government is giving up the fight for accessibility'
lead: Only 5 percent of the websites and apps of the Dutch government meet the accessibility requirements. Meanwhile, accessibility expert Jules Ernst sees some government websites even getting worse. 'A regulator was already promised in 2024, but nothing is happening.'

title: Asylum minister Van den Brink wants to punish asylum seeker who frustrates deportation
Arsenal loses its unbeaten status despite late goal in Munich, Jurriën Timber causes penalty
lead: Bayern Munich handed Arsenal their first points loss in the Champions League. The top match at the Allianz Arena ended in a draw: 2-2.

title: Dozens of civil servants still hired after Amsterdam municipality's vacancy freeze was supposed to be tightened 'with immediate effect'
Four dead in storms in France
lead: The severe weather in southern France and on the island of Corsica has already cost four people their lives, authorities in Bouches-du-Rhône say. Earlier, two fatalities had been reported. One person is also missing.

title: Bertram wants to combine public transport and other types of transport in the region
lead: Public transport and, among other things, pupil transport must be combined in regions where accessibility is declining. State Secretary <entity id="person:annet-bertram">Annet Bertram</entity> (Infrastructure, CDA) wants in this way to move from public transport to 'public mobility' that can be booked by everyone all day, she writes in a letter to the House of Representatives.

title: British government chases ultra-rich to Monaco and the Emirates, with their $160bn in wealth
lead: The relationship between the United Kingdom and billionaires is over. About fourteen have already left for greener tax pastures.

title: At this primary school, the children receive bilingual education. 'Handy if I become a professional footballer later'
Woman gives birth on train while on her way to a check-up at a Groningen hospital
lead: A woman gave birth on a train on Monday morning. She was on her way to a hospital in Groningen for a check-up when her waters suddenly broke, De Telegraaf reports.

title: Queen Máxima was set to listen to a pro-Palestinian band on 7 October, and then the visit was called off
lead: A working visit by <entity id="person:willem-alexander">koning Willem-Alexander</entity> and Queen Máxima is rarely cancelled at the last minute. Yet it happened earlier this month: Máxima was due to visit Poppodium 013 on, of all days, 7 October, with the pro-Palestinian band Droom Dit on the programme. Behind the scenes it is now said that this date was not a good choice for the visit.

title: Two ships sank in the Strait of Hormuz, containers floating at sea
lead: Two ships have sunk in the Strait of Hormuz. They were struck by something, but it is unclear whether it came from Iran. According to Iran, one of the ships hit a mine.
